name: Hubble Space Telescope
missionObjectives: Determine the expansion rate of the universe (Hubble Constant)
Study cosmic evolution and galaxies across deep time
Investigate stellar atmospheres and protoplanetary disks
Examine outer planet atmospheres and aurorae in our Solar System
majorDiscoveries: Measurement of Hubble Constant with high precision
Discovery of accelerating expansion of the universe driven by Dark Energy
Deep Field images revealing thousands of early galaxies
Confirmation of supermassive black holes at galaxy centers
majorAchievements: Over 30 years of continuous scientific operations
Five successful Space Shuttle servicing missions
Over 1.5 million observations enabling >20,000 scientific papers
timeline: 1990-04-24: Launched aboard Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-31)
1993-12-02: Servicing Mission 1 (COSTAR & WFPC2 installed to fix spherical aberration)
1997-02-11: Servicing Mission 2 (NICMOS & STIS installed)
1999-12-19: Servicing Mission 3A (Gyroscopes replaced)
2002-03-01: Servicing Mission 3B (ACS installed)
2009-05-11: Servicing Mission 4 (WFC3 & COS installed)
interestingFacts: Hubble completes an orbit around Earth roughly every 95 minutes at ~27,000 km/h.
It has no thrusters; attitude control relies entirely on reaction wheels and magnetic torquers.
description: The Hubble Space Telescope is a legendary space observatory launched in 1990 by NASA and ESA. Positioned above Earth's atmospheric distortion, Hubble provides ultra-sharp images from UV to near-IR wavelengths.

name: James Webb Space Telescope
instruments: Fine Guidance Sensor/Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph (FGS/NIRISS)
missionObjectives: Search for first light galaxies after the Big Bang
Determine how galaxies evolved from early formation to present
Observe star formation from initial stages to planetary systems
Measure physical and chemical properties of planetary systems & exoplanet atmospheres
majorDiscoveries: Detection of earliest known galaxies (redshift z > 14)
Detailed atmospheric transmission spectrum of exoplanet WASP-96b showing water vapor
Detection of CO2, SO2, and methane in exoplanet atmospheres
Observation of intricate dust and gas structures in Pillars of Creation and Carina Nebula
majorAchievements: Successful deployment of 18-segment gold-coated beryllium primary mirror in space
Deployment of 5-layer tennis-court-sized sunshield operating at ~40 Kelvin
Precision insertion into L2 halo orbit saving propellant for >20 years of operations
timeline: 2021-12-25: Launched aboard Ariane 5 from Kourou
2022-01-24: Successfully entered L2 halo orbit
2022-07-12: First scientific images released to the public
2023-09-11: Detection of carbon-bearing molecules in atmosphere of sub-Neptune exoplanet K2-18b
interestingFacts: JWST's primary mirror consists of 18 hexagonal segments coated in a thin layer of pure gold.
The sunshield keeps MIRI cooled down to just 6.7 Kelvin (-266°C) using a closed-cycle helium loop cryocooler.
description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is the premier space science observatory operated by NASA, ESA, and CSA. Designed to view the universe in infrared wavelengths, JWST unveils the first galaxies, star-forming regions, and exoplanetary atmospheres.

name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
missionObjectives: Observe high-energy X-ray emission from violent cosmic phenomena
Map hot gas in galaxy clusters to measure dark matter distribution
Study supernova remnants, neutron stars, and stellar black holes
Examine accretion disks around supermassive black holes
majorDiscoveries: Direct evidence of dark matter in the Bullet Cluster collision
Resolved diffuse X-ray background into individual active galactic nuclei
Observed the ring-like shockwaves of Supernova 1987A
Detected first X-ray emission from Sagittarius A*
majorAchievements: Sub-arcsecond angular resolution in X-rays, 25 times sharper than previous X-ray telescopes
Over 25 years of continuous X-ray astronomical observations
Pioneered high-resolution spatial and spectral X-ray imaging
timeline: 1999-07-23: Launched aboard Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-93)
1999-08-19: First light image of Cassiopeia A supernova remnant
2006-08-21: Discovery of dark matter in Bullet Cluster announced
interestingFacts: Named in honor of Nobel laureate Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar.
Chandra's mirrors are the smoothest ever constructed; if scaled to the size of Earth, the highest mountain would be less than 2 meters tall.
description: The Chandra X-ray Observatory is NASA's flagship X-ray telescope. Featuring high-precision grazing-incidence mirrors, Chandra inspects energetic phenomena such as black holes, neutron stars, and galaxy cluster collisions.

name: Spitzer Space Telescope
missionObjectives: Study cold circumstellar dust disks and brown dwarfs
Examine star-forming regions obscured by dust
Analyze atmosphere temperatures and compositions of extrasolar planets
Investigate ultraluminous infrared galaxies in the distant universe
majorDiscoveries: First direct detection of light from exoplanets (HD 209458b and TrES-1b)
Discovery of TRAPPIST-1 system's 7 Earth-sized exoplanets
Discovery of Saturn's giant, diffuse Phoebe ring
Characterization of dust and organic molecules in star-forming clouds
majorAchievements: Operated for 16.5 years (cold phase 2003-2009, warm phase 2009-2020)
Pioneered Earth-trailing heliocentric orbit to avoid Earth thermal background
Fundamental contributions to exoplanet atmospheric profiling
timeline: 2003-08-25: Launched aboard Delta II rocket
2005-03-22: First direct light captured from exoplanets
2009-05-15: Liquid helium coolant exhausted; start of Spitzer Warm Mission
2017-02-22: Discovery of seven Earth-size planets in TRAPPIST-1 system
2020-01-30: Mission officially decommissioned
interestingFacts: Spitzer was originally named SIRTF (Space Infrared Telescope Facility).
Its Earth-trailing orbit allowed it to drift about 0.1 AU per year away from Earth.
description: The Spitzer Space Telescope was the fourth and final element of NASA's Great Observatories program. Observing in thermal infrared, Spitzer imaged dusty starbirth regions, cool brown dwarfs, and exoplanet atmospheres.

name: Herschel Space Observatory
missionObjectives: Study galaxy formation in the early universe
Examine star formation and interaction with interstellar medium
Investigate chemical composition of atmospheres and surfaces of comets/planets
Analyze molecular chemistry of interstellar clouds
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of vast networks of interstellar filaments driving star formation
Detection of water vapor in comet Hartley 2 matching Earth's ocean water isotopic ratio
Mapped far-infrared emission of cool cosmic dust across thousands of galaxies
majorAchievements: Largest single single-mirror telescope operating in space until JWST
Pioneered submillimeter and far-infrared space astronomy
Completed over 35,000 scientific observations
timeline: 2009-05-14: Launched alongside Planck observatory on Ariane 5
2009-07-03: Reached L2 orbit
2013-04-29: Liquid helium coolant depleted, science operations concluded
interestingFacts: Its 3.5-meter mirror was manufactured from silicon carbide ceramic.
It carried over 2,300 liters of liquid helium coolant at 1.4 Kelvin.
description: The Herschel Space Observatory was an ESA space telescope operating in the far-infrared and submillimeter wavelengths. Equipped with a 3.5-meter primary mirror, Herschel peered through cold cosmic dust to study star formation.

name: Planck Space Observatory
missionObjectives: Map anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) with high angular resolution
Determine cosmological parameters (age, matter content, expansion rate) of the universe
Test inflationary models of the early universe
Map interstellar dust and magnetic fields in the Milky Way
majorDiscoveries: Refined universe age estimate to 13.82 billion years
Precisely determined universe composition: 68.3% Dark Energy, 26.8% Dark Matter, 4.9% Ordinary Matter
Definitive high-resolution sky map of CMB temperature and polarization fluctuations
majorAchievements: Highest-precision map of the Cosmic Microwave Background ever created
Operated HFI instrument cooled to 0.1 Kelvin (-273.05°C), the coldest known object in space
timeline: 2009-05-14: Launched alongside Herschel
2009-07-03: Arrived at L2
2013-03-21: First full-sky CMB data map released
2013-10-23: Decommissioned and safely parked in heliocentric disposal orbit
interestingFacts: Planck's HFI detectors operated at 0.1 K above absolute zero using an active dilution refrigerator.
description: Planck was an ESA space observatory dedicated to mapping the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation across the full sky with unprecedented sensitivity and angular resolution.

name: Gaia Space Observatory
missionObjectives: Construct the most precise 3D space catalog of nearly 2 billion stars in the Milky Way
Measure positions, parallaxes, and proper motions of celestial objects
Map radial velocities and chemical compositions of millions of stars
Detect thousands of exoplanets, asteroids, and quasars
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of Gaia-Enceladus (Sausage) ancient galaxy collision remnant
Mapping of the Milky Way spiral arm structure and warp in 3D
Cataloging position and motion of nearly 2 billion celestial objects (Data Release 3)
Identification of closest known black holes (Gaia BH1 and Gaia BH2)
majorAchievements: Created the largest, most accurate 3D map of our galaxy ever made
Achieved microarcsecond positional precision
Revolutionized Galactic dynamics, stellar evolution, and astrometry
timeline: 2013-12-19: Launched from French Guiana
2014-01-08: Entered orbit around Sun-Earth L2
2016-09-14: Gaia Data Release 1 (DR1)
2018-04-25: Gaia Data Release 2 (DR2)
2022-06-13: Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3)
interestingFacts: Gaia's focal plane contains 106 CCD sensors totaling nearly 1 billion pixels, the largest focal plane ever sent into space.
description: Gaia is an ESA astrometry space observatory tasked with creating a 3D optical catalog of almost 2 billion stars throughout the Milky Way galaxy, charting their position, motion, and brightness.

name: Hipparcos Space Astrometry Mission
missionObjectives: Measure precise trigonometric parallaxes, positions, and proper motions of >100,000 stars
Produce high-precision star catalogs for celestial navigation and astronomy
majorDiscoveries: Pinpointed distances to over 118,000 stars with 1 milliarcsecond precision (Hipparcos Catalogue)
Cataloged positions and brightness for over 2.5 million stars (Tycho-2 Catalogue)
majorAchievements: First space mission dedicated to precision astrometry
Laid the foundation for modern distance scales in astronomy
timeline: 1989-08-08: Launched on Ariane 44LP; apogee boost motor failed, leaving satellite in GTO
1993-08-15: Mission completed successfully despite unexpected orbit
1997-06-01: Hipparcos and Tycho Catalogs published
interestingFacts: Despite its boost motor failure leaving it in GTO, ESA engineers adapted communications stations to achieve 100% of mission scientific goals.
description: Hipparcos was an ESA space observatory launched in 1989. It was the world's first satellite dedicated to astrometry, producing the groundbreaking Hipparcos and Tycho star catalogs.

name: Kepler Space Telescope
missionObjectives: Survey Cygnus-Lyra region to determine frequency of Earth-size planets in habitable zones
Determine shapes and sizes of exoplanetary orbits
Estimate number of multi-planet systems around stars
majorDiscoveries: Discovered >2,600 confirmed exoplanets
Proved that planets outnumber stars in the Milky Way
Discovered Kepler-186f, the first Earth-sized planet in habitable zone of a red dwarf
Discovered Kepler-16b, the first circumbinary planet orbiting two stars
majorAchievements: Revolutionized exoplanetary science and planetary frequency estimates
Monitored >150,000 stars continuously for transit dips
timeline: 2009-03-07: Launched from Cape Canaveral
2013-05-11: Second reaction wheel failed; primary mission ended
2014-05-18: K2 extended mission approved
2018-10-30: Fuel exhausted; officially decommissioned
interestingFacts: Kepler pointed continuously at a single patch of sky containing 150,000 stars for over four years.
description: The Kepler Space Telescope was a NASA photometer designed to discover Earth-sized exoplanets orbiting other stars using the transit method.

name: K2 Mission (Second Light)
missionObjectives: Repurpose Kepler spacecraft using solar photon pressure to balance attitude
Survey target fields along the ecliptic plane in 80-day campaigns
Search for exoplanets around bright cool stars, star clusters, and Solar System bodies
majorDiscoveries: Discovered >500 additional confirmed exoplanets during 20 campaigns
Observed disintegrating exoplanet WD 1145+017 b orbiting a white dwarf
Observed super-flares on young solar-type stars and planetary transits in Hyades & Praesepe clusters
majorAchievements: Remarkable engineering recovery enabling 4 extra years of science after 2 reaction wheels failed
timeline: 2014-05-18: K2 mission official start
2018-10-30: Decommissioned upon final fuel depletion
interestingFacts: Engineers balanced the spacecraft against solar radiation pressure as a 'third reaction wheel'.
description: K2 was the second phase of the Kepler Space Telescope mission, modified to observe target fields along the ecliptic after reaction wheel degradation.

name: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite
instruments: Four Wide-Field Optical Cameras (16.8 megapixel CCDs each)
missionObjectives: Perform an nearly all-sky survey of bright, nearby stars to detect transiting exoplanets
Discover Earth and super-Earth-sized exoplanets suitable for atmospheric study by JWST
Provide targets for high-precision radial velocity follow-up
majorDiscoveries: Discovered >400 confirmed exoplanets and >7,000 candidate exoplanets
Discovered TOI-700 d and TOI-700 e, Earth-sized habitable zone planets
Captured first light transit of comet C/2018 N2 and stellar tidal disruption events (ASASSN-19bt)
majorAchievements: Mapped ~85% of the sky in 27-day sector strips
Pioneered a stable 2:1 lunar resonant high-Earth orbit
timeline: 2018-04-18: Launched on Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral
2018-05-17: Entered lunar resonant orbit (P/2)
2018-07-25: Science operations commenced
interestingFacts: TESS uses four identical custom cameras providing a total field of view of 24° × 96°.
Its orbit is highly stable and requires almost zero station-keeping fuel.
description: TESS is an all-sky transit survey space telescope designed to discover bright, nearby exoplanets for subsequent atmospheric characterization by the James Webb Space Telescope.

name: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer
missionObjectives: Perform an all-sky mid-infrared map with sensitivity 1000 times greater than IRAS
Discover ultracool Y-dwarfs and brown dwarfs
Catalog main-belt asteroids and near-Earth objects
majorDiscoveries: Discovered the coolest known class of brown dwarfs (Y-dwarfs)
Discovered Luhman 16, the third-closest star system to Earth
Discovered Earth's first Trojan asteroid (2010 TK7)
majorAchievements: Cataloged millions of infrared sources across the entire celestial sphere
Cryogenic coolant phase completed in October 2010
timeline: 2009-12-14: Launched from Vandenberg AFB
2010-10-05: Solid hydrogen coolant depleted
2011-02-17: Placed into hibernation (reactivated in 2013 as NEOWISE)
interestingFacts: WISE imaged the full sky 1.5 times during its primary cryogenic mission.
description: WISE was a NASA mid-infrared space telescope that surveyed the entire sky in four infrared wavelength bands, discovering brown dwarfs, distant ultraluminous galaxies, and asteroids.

name: NEOWISE (Near-Earth Object WISE)
missionObjectives: Search for and characterize near-Earth objects (NEOs), asteroids, and comets
Determine asteroid diameters and albedos using thermal infrared emission
Provide planetary defense early hazard detection
majorDiscoveries: Discovered comet C/2020 F3 (NEOWISE), one of the brightest naked-eye comets of the 21st century
Characterized >3,000 near-Earth objects and >158,000 asteroids across the Solar System
majorAchievements: Over 10 years of planetary defense infrared surveillance
Decommissioned in July 2024 due to atmospheric drag re-entry
timeline: 2013-09-13: Spacecraft reactivated as NEOWISE
2020-03-27: Discovery of comet C/2020 F3 (NEOWISE)
2024-07-31: Final science transmission; re-entered atmosphere late 2024
interestingFacts: NEOWISE used heat emitted by asteroids to accurately measure their physical sizes, unlike optical telescopes which only measure reflected light.
description: NEOWISE was a planetary defense space telescope mission created by reactivating the WISE spacecraft to detect and size near-Earth asteroids and comets in thermal infrared.

name: Euclid Space Telescope
missionObjectives: Map the 3D distribution of billions of galaxies across 10 billion light-years
Measure weak gravitational lensing to map Dark Matter distribution
Measure Baryonic Acoustic Oscillations to constrain Dark Energy
Test cosmic scale General Relativity modifications
majorDiscoveries: Released stunning first color images of Perseus Galaxy Cluster and Horsehead Nebula
Unveiled earliest full-sky survey test fields covering billions of distant galaxies
majorAchievements: High-precision 1.2m telescope delivering optical and near-IR wide-field imaging at L2
timeline: 2023-07-01: Launched on Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral
2023-07-28: Entered orbit around L2
2023-11-07: First scientific images released by ESA
interestingFacts: Euclid will map over one-third of the entire extragalactic sky, observing billions of galaxies.
description: Euclid is an ESA space telescope designed to map the geometry of the dark universe by measuring dark matter and dark energy through gravitational lensing and cosmic clustering.

name: Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer
instruments: Three Gas Pixel Detector (GPD) X-ray Polarimeters
missionObjectives: Measure X-ray polarization from cosmic sources (neutron stars, black holes, pulsars)
Map magnetic field geometry in supernova remnants and pulsar wind nebulae
Test general relativity in extreme gravitational fields near event horizons
majorDiscoveries: Mapped magnetic field structure of Cassiopeia A supernova remnant
Measured X-ray polarization of magnetar 4U 0142+61 revealing solid surface state
Determined geometry of corona and accretion disk around stellar black hole Cygnus X-1
majorAchievements: First dedicated X-ray polarimetry space observatory in 40 years
timeline: 2021-12-09: Launched on Falcon 9 into 0° inclination orbit
2022-01-11: First light image of Cassiopeia A
interestingFacts: IXPE uses a deployable 4-meter boom to separate its optics from its detectors.
description: IXPE is a NASA/ASI space observatory that measures the polarization of cosmic X-rays, uncovering the magnetic fields and geometries of extreme objects like black holes and magnetars.

name: Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array
instruments: Two Co-aligned Grazing-Incidence Hard X-ray Telescope Focal Plane Modules
missionObjectives: Survey supermassive black holes in active galactic nuclei
Map radioactive decay material in supernova remnants (Titanium-44)
Observe high-energy solar flare X-ray emissions
majorDiscoveries: First map of radioactive Titanium-44 in Cassiopeia A proving asymmetric explosion
Precise measurement of black hole spin in NGC 1365
Discovery of ultra-luminous X-ray pulsars exceeding Eddington limit by 100x
majorAchievements: First space telescope focusing high-energy / hard X-rays (3–79 keV)
Utilized 10-meter deployable mast for grazing optics focal length
timeline: 2012-06-13: Air-launched on Pegasus XL over Kwajalein Atoll
2012-06-21: 10-meter mast deployment completed
interestingFacts: NuSTAR was air-launched aboard a Pegasus XL rocket dropped from the belly of a Stargazer L-1011 aircraft.
description: NuSTAR is NASA's Small Explorer mission that pioneered hard X-ray focus imaging (3–79 keV) using 10-meter deployable optics to observe black holes, neutron stars, and supernova remnants.

name: Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory
missionObjectives: Detect and autonomously slew toward Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) within seconds
Determine GRB origins and physical mechanisms
Provide multi-wavelength follow-up of transient cosmic events
majorDiscoveries: Solved long-standing mystery of short GRBs, proving they originate from neutron star mergers
Detected farthest known GRB 090423 at redshift z = 8.2
Observed thousands of GRBs, supernovae, tidal disruption events, and comets
majorAchievements: Autonomous ultra-fast target repointing (<90 seconds)
Over 20 years of premier transient sky monitoring
timeline: 2004-11-20: Launched on Delta II
2005-05-09: First short GRB localization proving neutron star merger origin
2018-01-12: Renamed Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in honor of principal investigator
interestingFacts: Swift can automatically detect a gamma-ray burst and pivot its entire 1.5-ton structure in under 90 seconds.
description: The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is a multi-wavelength NASA space telescope built to catch transient cosmic explosions like gamma-ray bursts in real-time.

name: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
missionObjectives: Explore most energetic processes in the universe (supermassive black holes, pulsars, GRBs)
Search for signals of dark matter annihilation
Map high-energy cosmic rays and galactic gamma-ray emission
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of Fermi Bubbles: massive gamma-ray structures extending 25,000 light-years above and below galactic center
Detection of gamma-ray counterpart (GW170817) to binary neutron star gravitational wave merger
Cataloged hundreds of gamma-ray pulsars, including millisecond pulsars
majorAchievements: Full-sky gamma-ray coverage every three hours
Over 16 years of continuous high-energy survey science
timeline: 2008-06-11: Launched as GLAST; renamed Fermi shortly after launch
2010-11-09: Discovery of Fermi Bubbles announced
2017-08-17: Historic joint detection of GRB 170817A with LIGO/Virgo
interestingFacts: Fermi scans the entire sky every three hours, constantly updating the high-energy gamma-ray view of the cosmos.
description: Fermi is a NASA space observatory mapping the universe in high-energy gamma rays, uncovering extreme physics around pulsars, blazars, and dark matter.

name: XMM-Newton Observatory
missionObjectives: Perform high-sensitivity X-ray spectroscopy of cosmic sources
Study X-ray emission from hot intergalactic gas in galaxy clusters
Investigate supermassive black hole accretion dynamics and relativistic line broadening
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of relativistic iron K-alpha emission line broadening near black hole event horizons
Detected hot gas filaments connecting clusters in the cosmic web
Discovered X-ray flares from magnetars and young low-mass stars
majorAchievements: Over 25 years of operation; highest effective collecting area of any X-ray telescope
Pioneered simultaneous X-ray and optical/UV observations
timeline: 1999-12-10: Launched on inaugural commercial Ariane 5 rocket
2000-01-19: First light image of Large Magellanic Cloud
interestingFacts: XMM-Newton contains 174 nested high-precision gold mirrors split across three telescope modules.
description: XMM-Newton (X-ray Multi-Mirror Mission) is ESA's flagship X-ray observatory. With three large mirror modules, XMM-Newton captures energetic processes in stars, black holes, and galaxy clusters.

name: INTEGRAL (International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory)
instruments: Imager on Board the INTEGRAL Satellite (IBIS)
missionObjectives: Perform fine spectroscopy and imaging of gamma-ray sources (15 keV to 10 MeV)
Map radioactive isotopes from nucleosynthesis in supernovae (Aluminum-26)
Identify gamma-ray bursts and cosmic black hole candidates
majorDiscoveries: Mapped 1.8 MeV gamma-ray emission from radioactive Aluminum-26 across the Milky Way
Discovered new class of heavily obscured high-mass X-ray binary systems
Co-detected prompt gamma-ray emission from gravitational wave event GW170817
majorAchievements: Pioneered coded-aperture mask imaging in hard X-rays and gamma rays
Over 22 years of continuous gamma-ray observations
timeline: 2002-10-17: Launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome
2003-05-20: First full map of Galactic plane gamma-ray emission released
interestingFacts: Because gamma rays cannot be reflected by mirrors, INTEGRAL uses tungsten coded-aperture masks to cast shadows onto its detectors.
description: INTEGRAL is an ESA gamma-ray observatory dedicated to high-resolution imaging and spectroscopy of extreme cosmic phenomena, such as supernova nucleosynthesis and black holes.

name: Röntgen Satellite (ROSAT)
missionObjectives: Perform first high-resolution all-sky survey in soft X-rays (0.1–2.4 keV)
Catalog soft X-ray and extreme ultraviolet sources
Perform targeted pointing observations of X-ray sources
majorDiscoveries: Cataloged over 150,000 X-ray sources and 1,000 EUV sources
Discovered X-ray emission from comets (Comet Hyakutake in 1996)
Discovered isolated neutron stars (the 'Magnificent Seven')
majorAchievements: Revolutionized soft X-ray all-sky mapping
Discovered thermal X-ray emission from planetary and cometary atmospheres
timeline: 1990-06-01: Launched on Delta II rocket
1990-07-30: All-sky survey commenced
1999-02-12: Mission officially ended; re-entered Earth atmosphere in October 2011
interestingFacts: ROSAT surprised astronomers by discovering that comets emit bright soft X-rays due to solar wind charge exchange.
description: ROSAT was a German-led X-ray space telescope that performed the first imaging all-sky survey in soft X-rays and extreme ultraviolet wavelengths.

name: Infrared Astronomical Satellite
missionObjectives: Perform first un-obscured full-sky infrared survey at 12, 25, 60, and 100 μm
Catalog star-forming regions, dust clouds, and active galactic nuclei
majorDiscoveries: Discovered debris disk around Vega, first evidence of protoplanetary material around another star
Cataloged over 350,000 infrared sources
Discovered core of Milky Way galaxy obscured by dust
Discovered six comets (e.g. 126P/IRAS)
majorAchievements: First space observatory to perform an all-sky infrared survey
Mapped 96% of the sky in thermal infrared wavelengths
timeline: 1983-01-25: Launched from Vandenberg AFB
1983-11-21: Liquid helium cryogen exhausted, ending observations
interestingFacts: IRAS discovered a circumstellar dust disk around Vega, revealing that solar systems like ours could form around other stars.
description: IRAS was the first space-based observatory to perform an all-sky survey at infrared wavelengths, uncovering dust disks around stars and thousands of star-forming regions.

name: Cosmic Background Explorer
missionObjectives: Measure spectrum of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)
Detect spatial anisotropies / ripples in the CMB
Map diffuse cosmic infrared background radiation
majorDiscoveries: Confirmed CMB follows a precise blackbody spectrum with temperature T = 2.725 K
First detection of primordial temperature anisotropies (fluctuations) in CMB
Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to John Mather and George Smoot (2006)
majorAchievements: Provided definitive evidence supporting Big Bang theory
FIRAS spectrum is considered the most precise blackbody curve ever measured in nature
timeline: 1989-11-18: Launched on Delta rocket
1990-01-13: FIRAS blackbody result presented to AAS
1992-04-23: DMR anisotropy discovery announced
2006-10-03: Nobel Prize awarded to COBE principal investigators
interestingFacts: When COBE's FIRAS blackbody spectrum curve was shown at the AAS meeting in 1990, it matched theoretical prediction so perfectly that the audience gave a standing ovation.
description: COBE was a NASA space mission dedicated to studying the Cosmic Microwave Background. Its precise measurements confirmed the Big Bang theory's blackbody prediction and detected initial cosmic seeds.

name: Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe
missionObjectives: Map full-sky temperature anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background
Establish precise standard model of cosmology (Lambda-CDM)
Determine epoch of cosmic reionization and geometry of space
majorDiscoveries: Determined age of universe as 13.77 billion years (with 1% accuracy)
Established flat geometry of the universe (k = 0 within 0.4%)
Confirmed composition: 71.4% Dark Energy, 23.6% Dark Matter, 4.6% Baryonic Matter
Detected CMB polarization constraining first star formation (reionization)
majorAchievements: Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics (2018)
Transformed cosmology into a precision quantitative science
timeline: 2001-06-30: Launched on Delta II
2001-10-01: Entered L2 orbit
2003-02-11: First-year CMB results published
2010-08-19: Science operations concluded
interestingFacts: WMAP's full-sky CMB map became known as the 'baby picture of the Universe'.
description: WMAP was a NASA space mission operating at the Sun-Earth L2 point that mapped the temperature fluctuations of the Cosmic Microwave Background, establishing the Lambda-CDM model of cosmology.

name: Einstein Observatory (HEAO-2)
missionObjectives: First fully imaging X-ray telescope in space
Perform high-sensitivity imaging and spectroscopy of X-ray sources (0.2–20 keV)
majorDiscoveries: First true X-ray images of supernova remnants, pulsars, and active galaxies
Discovered X-ray coronae around normal stars
Resolved diffuse X-ray background in galaxy clusters
majorAchievements: Pioneered grazing-incidence Wolter Type I mirrors for X-ray astronomy
Renamed Einstein Observatory upon successful orbit insertion
timeline: 1978-11-13: Launched as HEAO-2; renamed Einstein Observatory
1981-04-25: Gas attitude control fuel exhausted
1994-03-25: Re-entered Earth atmosphere
interestingFacts: Einstein was the first satellite to take true focused X-ray images of astronomical targets.
description: The Einstein Observatory (HEAO-2) was the first fully imaging X-ray space telescope, launching grazing-incidence X-ray optics into astronomical research.

name: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory
missionObjectives: Perform comprehensive gamma-ray sky survey covering 20 keV to 30 GeV
Study gamma-ray bursts, active galactic nuclei, black holes, and pulsars
majorDiscoveries: BATSE proved that Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) are isotropically distributed, establishing cosmological origins
Discovered high-energy gamma-ray blazars emitting multi-GeV jets
Mapped Galactic 1.8 MeV Aluminum-26 gamma-ray line emission
majorAchievements: Second of NASA's Great Observatories program
Heaviest commercial astrophysics payload deployed by Space Shuttle at launch time (17 tons)
timeline: 1991-04-05: Deployed by STS-37 Atlantis
2000-06-04: Safely de-orbited into Pacific Ocean after gyro failure
interestingFacts: CGRO was intentionally de-orbited into the Pacific Ocean in 2000 to prevent uncontrolled re-entry after one of its gyroscopes failed.
description: The Compton Gamma Ray Observatory (CGRO) was the second of NASA's Great Observatories. CGRO covered six orders of magnitude in energy across gamma-ray astronomy, proving GRBs originate in distant deep space.

name: Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer
instruments: X-ray Timing Instrument (XTI: 56 Concentrator Optics & Silicon Drift Detectors)
missionObjectives: Measure radius and mass of neutron stars with 5% accuracy to constrain equation of state of ultra-dense matter
Perform sub-microsecond precision X-ray timing of millisecond pulsars
Demonstrate SEXTANT pulsar-based spacecraft navigation in space
majorDiscoveries: Precise radius measurement of millisecond pulsar PSR J0030+0451 revealing complex hot spots
Measured radius of heavy neutron star PSR J0740+6620 (2.08 Solar masses)
Demonstrated real-time autonomous X-ray pulsar navigation (SEXTANT)
majorAchievements: Operating mounted on ISS exterior for high-precision X-ray astrophysics
timeline: 2017-06-03: Launched aboard SpaceX CRS-11 to ISS
2017-06-14: Installed on ISS ELC-2 payload adapter
2017-11-01: SEXTANT autonomous pulsar navigation demonstration success
interestingFacts: NICER demonstrated that millisecond pulsars can serve as a cosmic GPS for deep space navigation.
description: NICER is an X-ray space telescope mounted on the International Space Station dedicated to studying the internal structure and equation of state of neutron stars through extreme precision timing.

name: X-ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission
missionObjectives: Perform ultra-high-resolution X-ray microcalorimeter spectroscopy of cosmic plasma
Measure velocities and kinetic energy of hot gas in galaxy clusters
Analyze abundance of heavy elements created by supernovae
majorDiscoveries: Resolved precise velocity structure and chemical composition of Perseus Cluster plasma
High-resolution X-ray spectrum of supernova remnant N132D in Large Magellanic Cloud
majorAchievements: Successful deployment of Resolve microcalorimeter operating at 50 mK (0.05 Kelvin)
Restored high-resolution X-ray microcalorimeter spectroscopy following Hitomi
timeline: 2023-09-06: Launched alongside SLIM moon lander from Tanegashima
2024-01-05: First light images and spectra released by JAXA and NASA
interestingFacts: XRISM's Resolve instrument measures X-ray energy by detecting tiny fractions of a degree in temperature change when a single X-ray photon strikes its detector cooled to 0.05 Kelvin.
description: XRISM is a joint JAXA/NASA X-ray space telescope equipped with an ultra-cold microcalorimeter spectrometer (Resolve) to study hot gas, galaxy clusters, and black hole feedback.

name: Spektr-RG Observatory
instruments: eROSITA (Extended Roentgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array)
missionObjectives: Perform ultra-deep all-sky survey in soft and hard X-rays
Discover ~100,000 galaxy clusters and millions of active galactic nuclei
Study large-scale structure evolution and dark energy
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of the eROSITA Bubbles: giant X-ray lobes extending above and below the Milky Way galactic plane
Cataloged over 1 million X-ray sources in first full-sky survey
majorAchievements: Deepest imaging X-ray all-sky survey ever conducted
timeline: 2019-07-13: Launched from Baikonur
2019-10-21: Reached L2 orbit
2020-06-19: First full-sky X-ray map completed
interestingFacts: Spektr-RG's eROSITA revealed giant X-ray bubbles towering thousands of light-years above and below the Milky Way's disk, similar to Fermi gamma-ray bubbles.
description: Spektr-RG is a Russian-German high-energy astrophysics space observatory stationed at L2, designed to conduct a deep all-sky survey in soft and hard X-rays.

name: AKARI (ASTRO-F)
missionObjectives: Perform high-resolution infrared all-sky survey across 1.7 to 180 μm
Study star formation, interstellar dust, and infrared galaxies
majorDiscoveries: Mapped 94% of the sky in far-infrared wavelengths
Cataloged over 1.3 million infrared sources in FIS and IRC catalogues
Detected water ice and organic molecules in star-forming regions and active galaxies
majorAchievements: Japan's first dedicated infrared space telescope mission
timeline: 2006-02-21: Launched on M-V rocket
2007-08-26: Liquid helium exhausted; warm mission continued in near-IR
2011-11-24: Decommissioned
interestingFacts: AKARI means 'light' in Japanese.
description: AKARI (ASTRO-F) was a JAXA infrared space telescope that surveyed the entire sky in near-, mid-, and far-infrared wavelengths.

name: Suzaku (ASTRO-E2)
instruments: X-ray Spectrometer (XRS - helium leak shortly after launch)
missionObjectives: Perform wide-band X-ray spectroscopy (0.2–600 keV) of energetic cosmic sources
Measure hot gas iron abundances in galaxy clusters
majorDiscoveries: Measured iron distribution in galaxy cluster outskirt gas
Observed broad iron K lines around spinning black holes
majorAchievements: Operated for over 10 years providing wide-band X-ray spectra
timeline: 2005-07-10: Launched as ASTRO-E2; renamed Suzaku
2015-09-02: Communication terminated; decommissioned
interestingFacts: Suzaku means 'Red Bird of the South' in Japanese mythology.
description: Suzaku (ASTRO-E2) was a joint JAXA/NASA X-ray space telescope providing broad-band spectroscopic observations of high-energy objects.
primaryDiscoveries: Galactic Cluster Outer Rim Iron Abundance

name: Hitomi (ASTRO-H)
missionObjectives: Demonstrate high-resolution X-ray microcalorimeter spectroscopy in space
Measure turbulence and motion of intergalactic gas in Perseus Cluster
majorDiscoveries: Measured motion of hot gas in Perseus Galaxy Cluster, showing surprisingly low turbulence
Proved revolutionary utility of X-ray microcalorimetry despite tragic short mission
majorAchievements: First operational X-ray microcalorimeter in orbit
timeline: 2016-02-17: Launched from Tanegashima
2016-02-25: High-resolution SXS observation of Perseus Cluster
2016-03-26: Attitude control software malfunction caused rapid rotation and break-up
interestingFacts: Hitomi means 'pupil of the eye' in Japanese.
Despite operating for only one month, Hitomi's observation of the Perseus Cluster resulted in landmark Nature papers.
description: Hitomi (ASTRO-H) was a JAXA/NASA X-ray observatory equipped with a revolutionary microcalorimeter. Although lost due to an attitude control software error, its measurement of the Perseus Cluster transformed astrophysics.

name: Astro-E2 (Suzaku Designator)
missionObjectives: Replacement satellite for ASTRO-E lost in 2000 launch failure
Perform wide-band X-ray spectroscopy of black holes and clusters
majorDiscoveries: Broadband X-ray spectral characterization of active galactic nuclei
majorAchievements: Successful replacement mission following Astro-E launch failure
timeline: 2005-07-10: Launched successfully and renamed Suzaku
interestingFacts: Astro-E2 was built as a direct copy and replacement of the Astro-E mission lost in 2000.
description: Astro-E2 was the pre-launch development designation for the Japanese Suzaku X-ray astronomy satellite.

name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
manufacturer: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Ball Aerospace
instruments: Wide Field Instrument (WFI - 300 megapixel infrared camera)
Coronagraph Instrument (CGI - starlight suppression technology demonstration)
missionObjectives: Survey wide field infrared sky with 100 times Hubble's field of view at Hubble resolution
Perform gravitational microlensing survey to discover thousands of rogue and bound exoplanets
Investigate dark energy physics through weak lensing and baryon acoustic oscillations
Demonstrate high-contrast coronagraphic direct imaging of exoplanets
majorDiscoveries: Mission in active development; targeted launch by May 2027
majorAchievements: 2.4-meter space telescope providing 100x Hubble's panoramic view
timeline: 2020-05-20: Officially renamed Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
2027-05-01: Target launch date aboard SpaceX Falcon Heavy
interestingFacts: A single Roman image will cover 100 times the sky area of a Hubble image with equal sharpness.
Named after Dr. Nancy Grace Roman, NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, known as the 'Mother of Hubble'.
description: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is a flagship NASA observatory designed to investigate dark energy, exoplanets via microlensing, and infrared survey astrophysics with a field of view 100x larger than Hubble.

name: Astrosat
missionObjectives: Simultaneous multi-wavelength monitoring of cosmic sources from UV to hard X-rays
Study high-energy processes in binary star systems, black holes, and neutron stars
Perform sky surveys in far and near ultraviolet bands
majorDiscoveries: Discovery of extreme UV light from galaxy AUDF01 located 9.3 billion light-years away
Detection of high-frequency X-ray oscillations in black hole binary GRS 1915+105
Measured hard X-ray polarization from the Crab Pulsar with CZTI
majorAchievements: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space astronomy observatory
Operating over 9 years, far exceeding design lifetime of 5 years
timeline: 2015-09-28: Launched by PSLV-C30 from Sriharikota
2015-10-05: First light observations from CZTI and UVIT instruments
2020-08-24: Discovery of deep-UV emission from galaxy AUDF01 published
interestingFacts: Astrosat is one of the few space observatories capable of simultaneous imaging from Far-UV (130 nm) up to hard X-rays (100 keV).
description: Astrosat is India's flagship multi-wavelength space observatory launched by ISRO. Equipped with UV and X-ray telescopes, Astrosat studies active galaxies, black holes, and starburst regions.
observationCapabilities: Simultaneous UV and X-ray Imaging & Spectroscopy

name: Galaxy Evolution Explorer
instruments: Far-Ultraviolet (FUV) & Near-Ultraviolet (NUV) Microchannel Plate Detector System
missionObjectives: Perform an all-sky ultraviolet survey to track star formation history across 10 billion years
Map UV emission of extragalactic systems and young hot star populations
majorDiscoveries: Discovered giant UV tail behind Mira (Omicron Ceti) extending 13 light-years
Mapped star formation in outer disks of spiral galaxies previously thought quiet
Cataloged over 200 million UV sources across the celestial sphere
majorAchievements: Premier space-based ultraviolet all-sky survey mission
timeline: 2003-04-28: Launched by Pegasus XL
2013-06-28: Decommissioned after 10 years of service
interestingFacts: GALEX revealed a massive comet-like tail of ejected gas trailing behind the star Mira, created by its speed through interstellar gas.
description: GALEX was a NASA space telescope observing the universe in ultraviolet light to measure the history of star formation across cosmic time.
observationCapabilities: Wide-field Far- and Near-UV Imaging & Spectroscopy

name: CHaracterising ExOPlanets Satellite
instruments: Ritchie-Chrétien Telescope with Frame-Transfer CCD Photometer
missionObjectives: Measure ultra-precise sizes of known exoplanets orbiting bright nearby stars
Determine bulk densities, compositions, and internal structures of super-Earths and sub-Neptunes
Select prime exoplanet candidates for atmospheric characterization by JWST
majorDiscoveries: Discovered football-shaped deformed exoplanet WASP-103b due to extreme tidal forces
Characterized planetary system LTT 9779 b, an ultra-hot Neptune with highly reflective metallic clouds
Discovered ring system around distant dwarf planet Quaoar outside its Roche limit
majorAchievements: First S-class mission in ESA's Cosmic Vision program
Sub-ppm ultra-high precision transit photometry
timeline: 2019-12-18: Launched on Soyuz from Kourou
2020-04-16: Commenced scientific operations
2023-03-07: Mission extended through 2026+
interestingFacts: CHEOPS does not search for new planets blindly; it targets known planet-hosting bright stars with extreme timing precision.
description: CHEOPS is an ESA space telescope dedicated to high-precision transit photometry of known exoplanets to accurately determine their radii, densities, and internal compositions.

name: PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars
instruments: Array of 26 Cameras (24 Normal Cameras & 2 Fast Cameras)
missionObjectives: Discover and characterize terrestrial exoplanets in habitable zone of Solar-type stars
Perform asteroseismology to determine precise ages and masses of host stars
Identify true Earth analogs orbiting Sun-like stars
majorDiscoveries: Targeted for launch in late 2026 to L2
majorAchievements: ESA M-class mission using multi-camera array design for wide field-of-view
timeline: 2014-02-19: Selected as ESA M3 mission
2026-12-01: Targeted launch date on Ariane 62
interestingFacts: PLATO will use 26 individual small telescopes mounted on a single platform to observe vast sky regions simultaneously.
description: PLATO is an ESA space telescope designed to discover Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of Sun-like stars while combining planet transit detection with stellar asteroseismology.

name: Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large-survey
missionObjectives: Perform chemical survey of 1,000 diverse exoplanet atmospheres
Measure chemical abundances, atmospheric temperatures, and cloud coverage
Understand planetary formation and chemical evolution ties to host stars
majorDiscoveries: Targeted launch in 2029 to Sun-Earth L2
majorAchievements: First space mission dedicated to systematic survey of exoplanet atmospheres
timeline: 2018-03-20: Selected as ESA M4 Cosmic Vision mission
2029-01-01: Targeted launch window aboard Ariane 62
interestingFacts: ARIEL will survey the atmospheres of 1,000 exoplanets ranging from hot Jupiters to super-Earths.
description: ARIEL is an ESA space telescope designed for a large-scale chemical survey of 1,000 exoplanetary atmospheres using infrared spectroscopy at the Sun-Earth L2 point.

name: Xuntian Chinese Space Station Telescope
instruments: Survey Camera (2.5 gigapixel focal plane array)
missionObjectives: Survey 40% of the sky in high-resolution optical and near-IR over 10 years
Study dark matter, dark energy, galaxy evolution, and AGN physics
Dock periodically with Tiangong Space Station for refueling and maintenance
majorDiscoveries: Targeted launch in 2026
majorAchievements: 2.0-meter space telescope featuring a field of view 300 times larger than Hubble
timeline: 2026-10-01: Targeted launch date aboard Long March 5B
interestingFacts: Xuntian can dock directly with China's Tiangong Space Station for in-orbit maintenance and instrument upgrades.
description: Xuntian (CSST) is a 2-meter optical space telescope developed by China. Operating in the same orbit as the Tiangong Space Station, Xuntian offers a field of view 300 times larger than Hubble.

name: CoRoT (Convection, Rotation and Planetary Transits)
missionObjectives: Search for transiting extrasolar planets (especially rocky planets)
Perform stellar asteroseismology to probe internal stellar structures
majorDiscoveries: Discovered CoRoT-7b, the first confirmed rocky exoplanet with measured density
Discovered 34 confirmed exoplanets and hundreds of candidate systems
Pioneered space-based asteroseismology across thousands of stars
majorAchievements: First space mission dedicated to exoplanet transit discovery
timeline: 2006-12-27: Launched from Baikonur
2009-02-03: Discovery of rocky exoplanet CoRoT-7b announced
2012-11-02: Instrument computer failure
2014-06-17: Decommissioned
interestingFacts: CoRoT-7b was the first exoplanet confirmed to be rocky like Earth, with a density matching rock and iron.
description: CoRoT was a French-led CNES/ESA space telescope pioneer that discovered the first confirmed rocky exoplanet (CoRoT-7b) using high-precision transit photometry.

name: Infrared Space Observatory
missionObjectives: Perform pointed infrared imaging, polarimetry, and spectroscopy from 2.5 to 240 μm
Study water and organic molecules in star-forming clouds and planetary atmospheres
majorDiscoveries: Discovered water vapor in star-forming regions, dying stars, and Titan's atmosphere
Detected crystalline silicates in circumstellar dust disks and comets
majorAchievements: Pioneered high-resolution infrared spectroscopy in space
timeline: 1995-11-17: Launched on Ariane 4
1998-04-08: Liquid helium coolant depleted
1998-05-16: Operations concluded
interestingFacts: ISO carried 2,280 liters of superfluid liquid helium to keep its instruments cooled to 1.8 Kelvin.
description: ISO was an ESA space observatory dedicated to infrared astronomy from 2.5 to 240 μm, uncovering interstellar water vapor and complex organic chemistry.

name: International Ultraviolet Explorer
missionObjectives: Observe ultraviolet spectra of celestial objects from comets to quasars
Monitor stellar activity, hot stars, and active galactic nuclei
majorDiscoveries: Monitored ultraviolet evolution of Supernova 1987A from day one
Discovered high-velocity winds in hot massive stars
Observed aurorae on Jupiter and Saturn and water loss rates from comets
majorAchievements: Operated continuously for over 18 years (originally planned for 3 years)
First astronomical satellite operated interactively by visiting scientists in real-time
timeline: 1978-01-26: Launched on Delta rocket
1987-02-24: Rapid response monitoring of Supernova 1987A
1996-09-30: Decommissioned after 18.5 years
interestingFacts: IUE was operated like a ground-based observatory: astronomers visited ground stations in Greenbelt (US) or Villafranca (Spain) to control it interactively.
description: IUE was a joint NASA/ESA/SERC ultraviolet space observatory that provided over 18 years of continuous UV spectroscopy for thousands of astronomical targets.

name: Orbiting Astronomical Observatory 3 (Copernicus)
instruments: Mullard Space Science Laboratory X-ray Experiment
missionObjectives: High-resolution ultraviolet absorption spectroscopy of interstellar gas
X-ray timing and spectroscopy of pulsars and X-ray binaries
majorDiscoveries: Discovered pervasive hot interstellar gas (T ~ 1 million K) heated by supernovae
Measured deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio in interstellar space confirming Big Bang nucleosynthesis models
Discovered X-ray pulsars such as X Persei
majorAchievements: Most successful early space telescope prior to Hubble
Operated for 8.5 years in orbit
timeline: 1972-08-21: Launched as OAO-3; renamed Copernicus
1981-02-15: Operations concluded
interestingFacts: Copernicus carried an 80 cm UV telescope mirror, making it the largest space telescope of its era.
description: OAO-3 (Copernicus) was a pioneering NASA space observatory that performed high-resolution UV spectroscopy of interstellar gas and early X-ray timing of compact objects.

name: Spektr-R (RadioAstron)
instruments: 10-meter Deployable Parabolic Radio Antenna (1.35, 6.2, 18, 92 cm receivers)
missionObjectives: Perform Space Very Long Baseline Interferometry (Space VLBI) in conjunction with ground radio telescopes
Achieve ultra-high angular resolution down to 8 microarcseconds
Image relativistic jets from active galactic nuclei and pulsar scattering disks
majorDiscoveries: Achieved highest angular resolution in history of astronomy (8 microarcseconds)
Discovered extremely high brightness temperatures in quasar cores exceeding theoretical Compton limit
Imaged compact central structures of blazar 3C 273 and galaxy M87
majorAchievements: Largest radio telescope antenna deployed in space (10 meters with 27 carbon-fiber petals)
timeline: 2011-07-18: Launched on Zenit-3F from Baikonur
2011-07-23: 10-meter parabolic dish successfully deployed
2019-01-10: Communications lost; mission declared complete May 2019
interestingFacts: By synthesizing data with ground radio dishes, RadioAstron created a virtual radio telescope almost 350,000 km across—nearly the distance to the Moon.
description: Spektr-R (RadioAstron) was a Russian space VLBI radio observatory featuring a 10-meter deployable parabolic dish that achieved the sharpest angular resolution in astronomical history.

name: HALCA (VSOP / Haruka)
instruments: 8-meter Deployable Mesh Radio Reflector (1.6, 5, 22 GHz receivers)
missionObjectives: Perform Space Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VSOP project)
Image radio jets in active galactic nuclei with sub-milliarcsecond resolution
majorDiscoveries: Imaged core structure and magnetic field bending in quasar M87 and 3C 279
Proved feasibility of orbital space VLBI synthesizing baselines 3x Earth diameter
majorAchievements: First satellite dedicated to Space VLBI radio astronomy
timeline: 1997-02-12: Launched on maiden flight of M-V rocket; named Haruka
1997-02-28: 8-meter mesh antenna successfully deployed
2005-11-30: Mission officially concluded
interestingFacts: HALCA's 8-meter dish was constructed from gold-plated wire mesh deployed by six inflatable struts.
description: HALCA (Haruka) was a Japanese space VLBI radio telescope equipped with an 8-meter mesh dish that joined ground radio arrays to synthesize giant interplanetary-scale radio baselines.
primaryDiscoveries: First Orbital Space VLBI Images of Quasars

name: Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer
instruments: Four Rowland Circle Grating Spectrographs (90.5–118.7 nm)
missionObjectives: Perform high-resolution spectroscopic study of far-ultraviolet wavelengths (90.5–118.7 nm)
Measure abundance of deuterium created during Big Bang nucleosynthesis
Map hot O VI gas in the halo of the Milky Way galaxy
majorDiscoveries: Precision measurement of cosmic deuterium abundance validating Big Bang models
Discovered extensive hot O VI gas halo surrounding the Milky Way
Detected molecular hydrogen in circumstellar disks around young stars
majorAchievements: Pioneered far-UV spectroscopy below Hubble's 115 nm optical cutoff
timeline: 1999-06-24: Launched on Delta II
2007-10-18: Mission officially terminated after reaction wheel failures
interestingFacts: FUSE observed spectral lines of molecular hydrogen and deuterium that cannot be observed from the ground or by Hubble due to atmospheric and optical mirror cutoffs.
description: FUSE was a NASA space observatory dedicated to high-resolution spectroscopy in the far-ultraviolet spectrum (90.5–118.7 nm), measuring primordial deuterium and hot galactic gas.

name: Submillimeter Wave Astronomy Satellite
missionObjectives: Study galactic molecular clouds by measuring spectral lines of water (H2O), isotopic water, molecular oxygen (O2), neutral carbon (C I), and carbon monoxide (CO)
Understand cooling mechanisms in collapsing star-forming clouds
majorDiscoveries: Found surprisingly low water vapor and O2 abundances in cold interstellar gas clouds
Observed water release from comet Deep Impact strike on Comet Tempel 1 in 2005
majorAchievements: Pioneered submillimeter spectral line survey techniques in space
timeline: 1998-12-05: Launched on Pegasus XL
2004-07-21: Hibernation phase started
2005-07-04: Reactivated briefly to support Deep Impact comet encounter
interestingFacts: SWAS was woken up from hibernation in 2005 specifically to watch NASA's Deep Impact probe blast a crater into Comet Tempel 1.
description: SWAS was a NASA Small Explorer space observatory operating in the submillimeter wave spectrum to map molecular water and oxygen in interstellar clouds.

name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory
instruments: Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO C2/C3)
missionObjectives: Investigate solar interior structure via helioseismology
Study solar corona heating and dynamics
Monitor coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and solar wind origin for space weather forecasting
majorDiscoveries: Discovered >5,000 sungrazing comets (most prolific comet hunter in history)
Revolutionized helioseismology mapping solar subsurface convection flows
Discovered origin of fast solar wind from magnetic coronal holes
majorAchievements: Over 30 years of continuous solar surveillance at L1
Critical operational space weather warning sentinel for Earth
timeline: 1995-12-02: Launched on Atlas IIAS from Cape Canaveral
1996-02-14: Entered halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1
1998-06-25: Temporarily lost attitude control; recovered by joint team in September 1998
2024-03-25: SOHO discovered its 5,000th comet
interestingFacts: SOHO is the most successful comet finder in human history, discovering over 5,000 comets using citizen science.
description: SOHO is an ESA/NASA solar space observatory positioned at Sun-Earth L1. SOHO maps the Sun's deep interior, corona, and coronal mass ejections while discovering thousands of comets.

name: Solar Dynamics Observatory
instruments: Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA - 4 telescopes imaging 10 wavelengths)
missionObjectives: Understand solar magnetic field generation, structure, and conversion into explosive events (flares & CMEs)
Provide ultra-high cadence full-disk imaging of the Sun in 4K resolution every 12 seconds
majorDiscoveries: Revealed fine-scale magnetic reconnection mechanisms in solar flares
Mapped global solar magnetic field changes across complete 11-year solar cycles
Observed transit of Venus across the Sun in 2012 in extreme UV
majorAchievements: Transmits 1.5 terabytes of ultra-high-definition solar data back to Earth every day
Continuous 24/7 solar imaging coverage from geosynchronous orbit
timeline: 2010-02-11: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2010-04-21: First light images released
2012-06-05: Historic observation of Transit of Venus
interestingFacts: SDO streams full 4096×4096 resolution 4K images of the Sun every 12 seconds, generating over 1.5 TB of raw data per day.
description: The Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) is a flagship NASA heliophysics space telescope operating in geosynchronous orbit to monitor solar magnetic fields, flares, and solar atmosphere dynamics.

name: Voyager 1
missionObjectives: Perform close flybys of Jupiter and Saturn systems including Titan
Investigate planetary magnetic fields, atmosphere dynamics, and ring structures
Explore outer boundary of heliosphere and penetrate interstellar medium
majorDiscoveries: First observation of active volcanism outside Earth on Jupiter's moon Io
Discovery of intricate ring structures, spokes, and shear waves in Saturn's rings
First human-made object to cross heliopause into interstellar space (August 25, 2012)
Captured iconic 'Pale Blue Dot' image of Earth from 6 billion km away in 1990
majorAchievements: Farthest human-made object from Earth (>160 AU / 24 billion km)
Over 48 years of continuous active operation powered by RTGs
Carries the Golden Record containing Earth's sounds, music, and images
timeline: 1977-09-05: Launched from Cape Canaveral
1979-03-05: Closest approach to Jupiter (280,000 km)
1980-11-12: Closest approach to Saturn and Titan
1990-02-14: Captured 'Solar System Family Portrait' including Pale Blue Dot
2012-08-25: Crossed heliopause into interstellar space
interestingFacts: Voyager 1's signals travelling at light speed take over 22.5 hours to reach Earth.
It carries a 12-inch gold-plated copper phonograph record containing 115 images, greetings in 55 languages, and natural Earth sounds.
description: Voyager 1 is a NASA deep space probe launched in 1977. Having explored Jupiter and Saturn, it became the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space in 2012.

name: Voyager 2
missionObjectives: Execute Planetary Grand Tour of outer giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune
Examine atmosphere, rings, and magnetospheres of gas and ice giants
Penetrate interstellar space following heliopause crossing
majorDiscoveries: Only spacecraft in history to visit Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989)
Discovered active nitrogen geysers on Neptune's moon Triton
Discovered 10 new moons of Uranus and 6 new moons of Neptune
Discovered Neptune's Great Dark Spot and high-speed atmospheric winds (up to 2,100 km/h)
Entered interstellar space on November 5, 2018
majorAchievements: Completed the full 'Grand Tour' of all four outer giant planets
Over 48 years of continuous active operation powered by RTGs
timeline: 1977-08-20: Launched 16 days before Voyager 1
1979-07-09: Closest approach to Jupiter
1981-08-26: Closest approach to Saturn
1986-01-24: First and only spacecraft flyby of Uranus
1989-08-25: First and only spacecraft flyby of Neptune and Triton
2018-11-05: Crossed heliopause into interstellar space
interestingFacts: Voyager 2 launched 16 days before Voyager 1 on a trajectory that allowed it to visit Uranus and Neptune.
It is the only spacecraft to have imaged Uranus and Neptune up close.
description: Voyager 2 is a NASA deep space probe launched in 1977. It completed a historic Grand Tour of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, and entered interstellar space in 2018.

name: Pioneer 10
missionObjectives: First spacecraft to traverse the Asteroid Belt and fly by Jupiter
Measure radiation environment and magnetic field of Jupiter
Obtain first close-up images of Jupiter and its Galilean moons
majorDiscoveries: Proved that crossing the Asteroid Belt poses low collision hazard to spacecraft
Mapped intense radiation belts and magnetic envelope surrounding Jupiter
Captured first close-up optical images of Jupiter and Galilean moons
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to cross the Asteroid Belt and fly by Jupiter (1973)
First human-made object on a solar system escape trajectory
Carried the famous gold-anodized Pioneer Plaque
timeline: 1972-03-03: Launched from Cape Canaveral
1972-07-15: Entered Asteroid Belt
1973-12-04: Historic closest approach to Jupiter (132,200 km)
1983-06-13: Passed orbit of Neptune, becoming most distant human-made object at that time
2003-01-23: Final weak signal received at distance of 82 AU
interestingFacts: Pioneer 10 carries a gold-anodized aluminum plaque depicting a man, woman, and diagram of Earth's position relative to pulsars.
description: Pioneer 10 was a milestone NASA deep space probe launched in 1972. It was the first spacecraft to navigate the Asteroid Belt, fly by Jupiter, and achieve solar escape velocity.

name: Pioneer 11
missionObjectives: Perform close flyby of Jupiter and use gravity assist to fly by Saturn
Perform first close-up exploration of Saturn and its rings
Test Saturn ring particle density prior to Voyager encounters
majorDiscoveries: First spacecraft to visit Saturn (1979), discovering Saturn's F Ring and moon Epimetheus
Mapped Saturn's magnetic field and radiation environment
Discovered that Titan has an extremely cold nitrogen-dominated atmosphere
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to encounter Saturn
Pioneered complex Jupiter gravity assist maneuver to bend trajectory toward Saturn
timeline: 1973-04-06: Launched from Cape Canaveral
1974-12-02: Closest approach to Jupiter (42,800 km)
1979-09-01: Historic first flyby of Saturn (21,000 km)
1995-09-30: Final science operations terminated
interestingFacts: Pioneer 11 flew within 21,000 km of Saturn's cloud tops, passing directly through the ring plane to pave a safe path for Voyager.
description: Pioneer 11 was a NASA space probe that executed a Jupiter gravity assist to achieve the first flyby of Saturn in 1979, discovering the F Ring.

name: New Horizons
instruments: Ralph (Multispectral Visible Imager & Infrared Spectrometer MVIC/LEISA)
PEPSSI (Pluto Energetic Particle Spectrometer Science Investigation)
missionObjectives: Perform first reconnaissance flyby of Pluto and its moons (Charon, Styx, Nix, Kerberos, Hydra)
Map global surface composition, geology, and atmosphere of Pluto
Fly by a classical Kuiper Belt Object (KBO) to explore primitive outer solar system building blocks
majorDiscoveries: Revealed Pluto to be a geologically active world with nitrogen ice glaciers (Sputnik Planitia) and cryovolcanoes
Discovered Charon's dark reddish polar cap (Mordor Macula) composed of tholins
First close-up flyby of contact binary Kuiper Belt Object 486958 Arrokoth (Ultima Thule) on January 1, 2019
majorAchievements: Fastest spacecraft departure from Earth at launch (16.26 km/s / 58,536 km/h)
Explored the most distant solid object ever visited by a spacecraft (Arrokoth at 44 AU)
timeline: 2006-01-19: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2007-02-28: Jupiter gravity assist flyby
2015-07-14: Historic closest approach to Pluto (12,500 km)
2019-01-01: Historic flyby of Kuiper Belt Object 486958 Arrokoth
interestingFacts: New Horizons carried some of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, the astronomer who discovered Pluto in 1930.
description: New Horizons is a NASA space probe that conducted the first flyby reconnaissance of Pluto and its moons in 2015, and the distant Kuiper Belt Object Arrokoth in 2019.

name: Cassini–Huygens Mission
missionObjectives: Perform comprehensive orbital exploration of Saturn, its rings, and magnetosphere
Deploy Huygens probe to land on surface of moon Titan
Investigate subsurface ocean icy moons Enceladus and Titan
majorDiscoveries: Discovered active saltwater geysers erupting from subsurface ocean of icy moon Enceladus
Huygens landing on Titan revealed liquid methane/ethane lakes, rivers, and organic dunes
Discovered propeller structures, hexagonal polar jet stream, and ring dynamic waves at Saturn
Discovered new moons (Methone, Pallene, Polydeuces, Daphnis, Aegaeo, Anthe)
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit Saturn (13 years of orbit)
Huygens landing: farthest landing from Earth ever accomplished (Titan)
Grand Finale: 22 daring dives between Saturn and its innermost rings before plunging into atmosphere
timeline: 1997-10-15: Launched on Titan IVB
2004-07-01: Saturn Orbit Insertion (SOI)
2005-01-14: ESA Huygens probe successfully landed on Titan
2005-07-14: First close flyby of Enceladus discovering cryovolcanic plumes
2017-09-15: Cassini 'Grand Finale' atmospheric entry into Saturn
interestingFacts: Huygens landed on Titan's surface in 2005, sending back pictures of rounded ice pebbles and liquid hydrocarbon riverbeds 1.4 billion km from Earth.
description: Cassini–Huygens was a flagship NASA/ESA/ASI mission to Saturn. Cassini spent 13 years orbiting Saturn while ESA's Huygens probe performed the farthest surface landing in human history on Titan.

name: Galileo Spacecraft
missionObjectives: First long-term orbital investigation of Jupiter and its Galilean moons
Deploy atmospheric probe directly into Jupiter's dense atmosphere
Investigate subsurface ocean evidence on Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto
majorDiscoveries: Strong evidence for liquid water ocean beneath Europa's icy crust
Discovered Ganymede possesses its own intrinsic magnetic field (only moon known to have one)
First spacecraft to discover an asteroid moon (Dactyl orbiting asteroid 243 Ida)
Observed collision of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 with Jupiter in 1994
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit Jupiter (1995–2003)
First atmospheric descent probe deployed into a giant gas planet
timeline: 1989-10-18: Deployed by STS-34 Atlantis
1993-08-28: Discovered Dactyl orbiting asteroid Ida
1995-12-07: Probe descended into Jupiter; Galileo orbiter entered Jovian orbit
2003-09-21: Intentionally plunged into Jupiter to prevent contamination of Europa
interestingFacts: Galileo's high-gain main antenna failed to unfurl; JPL engineers re-wrote flight software to compress data over the low-gain antenna, saving the mission.
description: Galileo was NASA's landmark mission to Jupiter, consisting of an orbiter and atmospheric probe. It uncovered evidence of liquid oceans on Europa and Ganymede's magnetic field.

name: Juno Spacecraft
missionObjectives: Investigate Jupiter's core mass, internal composition, and deep atmospheric water content
Map Jupiter's intense gravitational and magnetic fields with unprecedented precision
Explore polar magnetosphere and intense polar aurorae
majorDiscoveries: Discovered stable geometric clusters of persistent cyclones at Jupiter's north and south poles
Revealed Jupiter's core is dilute and fuzzy, extending across nearly half the planet's radius
Mapped powerful dynamic auroral electron beams and shallow lightning in upper atmosphere
majorAchievements: Farthest solar-powered spacecraft operating in deep space
Closest polar orbits of Jupiter in history (perijove ~4,200 km above cloud tops)
timeline: 2011-08-05: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2016-07-04: Successfully entered polar orbit around Jupiter
2021-06-07: Extended mission flyby of Ganymede
2022-09-29: Close flyby of Europa (352 km)
2023-12-30: Extremely close flyby of volcanic moon Io (1,500 km)
interestingFacts: Juno is powered by three massive solar panels extending 20 meters across, producing electricity at Jupiter where sunlight is 25 times weaker than at Earth.
description: Juno is a NASA solar-powered planetary orbiter exploring Jupiter from a highly elliptical polar orbit to probe its interior structure, magnetic field, and polar atmosphere.

name: Dawn Spacecraft
missionObjectives: Explore the two largest bodies in the main asteroid belt: protoplanet Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres
Determine building blocks of protoplanetary formation in early Solar System
Examine surface composition, water ice distribution, and internal differentiation
majorDiscoveries: Discovered bright sodium carbonate deposits (Occator Crater faculae) on dwarf planet Ceres
Found evidence of brine subsurface reservoirs and active cryovolcanism (Ahuna Mons) on Ceres
Mapped Vesta's massive south polar impact basin Rheasilvia and central mountain twice as tall as Mt. Everest
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit two different extraterrestrial bodies
First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid in the main belt (Vesta) and first to visit a dwarf planet (Ceres)
Pioneered ion propulsion for deep space exploration
timeline: 2007-09-27: Launched on Delta II
2011-07-16: Entered orbit around Vesta
2012-09-05: Departed Vesta for Ceres
2015-03-06: Entered orbit around dwarf planet Ceres
2018-11-01: Hydrazine fuel exhausted; left in stable permanent orbit around Ceres
interestingFacts: Dawn's xenon ion engines operated for over 5.9 years (51,472 hours), providing a total velocity change (delta-v) of 11.5 km/s—more than any spacecraft propulsion system in history.
description: Dawn was a NASA space probe propelled by ion engines that achieved orbit around protoplanet Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres, uncovering active cryovolcanism and ice.

name: MESSENGER (MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging)
missionObjectives: Perform first complete global orbital mapping of planet Mercury
Determine composition of Mercury's surface and high-density metallic core size
Search for water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters
majorDiscoveries: Confirmed abundant water ice and organic compounds buried inside permanently shadowed polar craters
Discovered unusual surface hollows created by volatile sublimation
Discovered Mercury's offset magnetic field and unexpectedly large iron-rich core
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit planet Mercury (2011–2015)
Completed 4,105 orbits around Mercury
timeline: 2004-08-03: Launched from Cape Canaveral
2011-03-18: Mercury Orbit Insertion (MOI)
2012-11-29: Confirmation of polar water ice announced
2015-04-30: Intentionally impacted surface of Mercury at 14,000 km/h after propellant exhaustion
interestingFacts: MESSENGER used a protective ceramic sunshade curtain to operate safely at temperatures reaching 370°C near Mercury.
description: MESSENGER was a NASA space probe that became the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury, revealing polar water ice, volcanic smooth plains, and an offset magnetic field.

name: Magellan Spacecraft (Venus Radar Mapper)
missionObjectives: Map 98% of the surface of Venus using high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)
Construct topographically accurate global radar maps through dense cloud shroud
Measure gravity field of Venus
majorDiscoveries: Mapped 98% of Venus surface at resolutions better than 150 meters
Revealed Venus is covered in widespread volcanic features, pancake domes, and lava channels
Proved absence of Earth-like plate tectonics on Venus
majorAchievements: First interplanetary mission launched from a Space Shuttle
Pioneered aerobraking maneuvers in a planetary atmosphere to circularize orbit
timeline: 1989-05-04: Launched aboard Atlantis (STS-30)
1990-08-10: Entered Venus orbit
1994-10-13: Plunged into Venus atmosphere (Project Windmill)
interestingFacts: Magellan used spare parts leftover from Voyager, Galileo, Ulysses, and Mariner 9 to lower construction cost.
description: Magellan was a NASA space probe that mapped 98% of Venus's surface with Synthetic Aperture Radar, revealing volcanoes and lava plains.

name: Venus Express
instruments: Visible and Infrared Thermal Imaging Spectrometer (VIRTIS)
SPICAV / SOIR (Spectrometer for Infrared & UV Absorption)
missionObjectives: Study complex atmosphere dynamics, super-rotation, and greenhouse effect on Venus
Search for present-day active volcanism on Venus surface
Examine solar wind interaction and atmospheric escape rates
majorDiscoveries: Detected transient thermal hotspots on Venus surface matching active lava flows
Discovered double-eyed atmospheric vortex at Venus's south pole
Detected ozone layer in upper atmosphere of Venus
majorAchievements: ESA's first mission to planet Venus
Operated for 9 years in orbit, concluding with high-altitude aerobraking experiments
timeline: 2005-11-09: Launched from Baikonur
2006-04-11: Venus Orbit Insertion
2014-12-16: Propellant exhausted following experimental aerobraking campaign
interestingFacts: Venus Express reused spacecraft design elements from ESA's Mars Express mission to save development time.
description: Venus Express was ESA's first mission to Venus. It studied Venus's dense atmosphere, super-rotating winds, and detected evidence of recent active volcanism.

name: Akatsuki (PLANET-C / Venus Climate Orbiter)
missionObjectives: Study atmospheric dynamics and 4-day super-rotation of Venus
Search for Venusian lightning and active volcanism
Map cloud structures at multiple atmospheric altitudes
majorDiscoveries: Discovered massive stationary gravity wave 10,000 km long stretching across Venus's upper atmosphere
Mapped high-speed jet streams and equatorial cloud circulation patterns
majorAchievements: Miraculous orbit recovery: entered Venus orbit in 2015 using RCS thrusters 5 years after main engine failure
timeline: 2010-05-20: Launched from Tanegashima
2010-12-06: Main engine failed during orbit insertion; missed Venus
2015-12-07: Successful orbit insertion using attitude control thrusters 5 years later
interestingFacts: JAXA engineers spent 5 years orbiting the Sun waiting for Akatsuki to catch Venus again after its main engine failed.
description: Akatsuki is a JAXA Venus climate orbiter that successfully recovered from a main engine failure to map Venus's atmospheric super-rotation and massive gravity waves.

name: Mars Express
instruments: MARSIS (Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding)
OMEGA (Visible and Infrared Mineralogical Mapping Spectrometer)
missionObjectives: Perform high-resolution 3D color imaging of Mars surface
Probe subsurface geological layers and search for underground ice/water deposits
Map mineral composition of Martian terrain
majorDiscoveries: MARSIS radar detected evidence of liquid water lake beneath south polar ice cap (Planum Australe)
Mapped widespread clay minerals (phyllosilicates) proving early Mars had abundant liquid water
Confirmed presence of water ice deposits at Martian south pole
majorAchievements: ESA's first planetary mission (over 21 years in active orbit around Mars)
timeline: 2003-06-02: Launched on Soyuz from Baikonur
2003-12-25: Mars Orbit Insertion; Beagle 2 lander deployed (lost on surface)
2018-07-25: Discovery of subglacial liquid lake on Mars announced
interestingFacts: Mars Express's HRSC camera has mapped virtually the entire surface of Mars in 3D color.
description: Mars Express is ESA's long-running Mars orbiter. Equipped with HRSC 3D imaging and MARSIS subsurface radar, it discovered subsurface liquid water reservoirs and hydrated minerals.

name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
missionObjectives: Map chemical elements and minerals across Mars surface
Search for subsurface water ice deposits
Serve as primary communications relay for Mars rovers (Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance)
majorDiscoveries: Discovered vast shallow deposits of subsurface water ice across high Martian latitudes
Global thermal infrared mineral mapping of Mars
Monitored radiation environment for future human exploration
majorAchievements: Longest-continually-surviving spacecraft in orbit around another planet (>24 years)
Relayed >85% of all data from NASA Mars rovers and landers back to Earth
timeline: 2001-04-07: Launched on Delta II
2001-10-24: Mars Orbit Insertion
2002-05-28: Discovery of vast polar water ice deposits published
interestingFacts: Mars Odyssey holds the world record for the longest continuously operating spacecraft in orbit around any planet other than Earth.
description: 2001 Mars Odyssey is NASA's longest-running Mars orbiter. It discovered vast shallow subsurface water ice and acts as the chief communications relay for Mars rovers.

name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
instruments: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE - 0.5m telescope)
Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM)
missionObjectives: Perform ultra-high-resolution imaging of Martian surface features (30 cm per pixel)
Search for evidence of past liquid water environments and landing sites for rovers
Radar probe shallow subsurface ice sheets and glaciers
majorDiscoveries: HiRISE imaged Recurring Slope Lineae (RSL) seasonal dark streaks suggesting salty liquid flows
Discovered massive pure underground ice sheets exposed at cliff scarps
Imaged active avalanche drops, dust devils, and landing site terrain for Curiosity & Perseverance
majorAchievements: Returned more data than all other deep-space missions combined
Over 20 years of ultra-high-resolution Martian reconnaissance
timeline: 2005-08-12: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2006-03-10: Mars Orbit Insertion
2006-11-01: Primary science phase started after aerobraking
interestingFacts: MRO's HiRISE camera can resolve objects as small as a dinner plate on the surface of Mars from 300 km altitude.
description: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) is a NASA spacecraft providing ultra-high-resolution 30 cm/pixel imaging (HiRISE) and subsurface radar sounding of Mars.

name: MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN)
instruments: Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer (NGIMS)
missionObjectives: Measure rate of atmospheric loss to space caused by solar wind stripping
Determine role of atmospheric escape in transforming Mars from warm/wet to cold/dry
Study upper atmosphere structure and ionosphere solar interactions
majorDiscoveries: Measured solar wind stripping rate: Mars loses ~100 grams of atmosphere to space every second
Discovered proton aurorae and widespread metal ion layers in upper atmosphere
Proved solar storms dramatically accelerate atmospheric loss rate by over 10x
majorAchievements: First spacecraft dedicated to exploring upper atmosphere of Mars
timeline: 2013-11-18: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2014-09-22: Mars Orbit Insertion
2015-11-05: Discovery of solar wind atmospheric stripping rate announced
interestingFacts: MAVEN proved that solar wind stripping stripped away most of Mars's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere over billions of years after its magnetic field died.
description: MAVEN is a NASA Mars orbiter dedicated to measuring the upper atmosphere and solar wind erosion rate to understand how Mars lost its atmosphere and surface water.

name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
instruments: NOMAD (Nadir and Occultation for MArs Discovery Spectrometer)
CASSIS (Colour and Stereo Surface Imaging System)
missionObjectives: Detect trace atmospheric gases (methane, water vapor, ozone) down to parts-per-trillion levels
Map surface hydrogen/water-ice distribution down to 1 meter depth
Provide high-resolution stereo surface imaging and data relay for Rosalind Franklin rover
majorDiscoveries: Discovered massive shallow water ice reserves in Valles Marineris canyon system (Canyon Water)
Set strict upper limits on Martian methane presence (<0.05 ppb)
Detected glowing green nightglow in Martian upper atmosphere
majorAchievements: Highest-sensitivity atmospheric chemistry suite in Martian orbit
Successful 1-year aerobraking campaign to reach 400 km science orbit
timeline: 2016-03-14: Launched on Proton-M from Baikonur
2016-10-19: TGO Orbit Insertion; Schiaparelli lander lost during landing
2018-04-09: Science observations commenced following aerobraking
interestingFacts: TGO's FREND instrument detected water ice beneath the floor of Valles Marineris canyon system, covering an area the size of the Netherlands.
