description: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) is a joint ESA/Roscosmos mission studying rare atmospheric gases on Mars while mapping subsurface water ice deposits.

name: Tianwen-1 Orbiter
missionObjectives: Perform global remote sensing of Mars geology, topography, and surface soil structure
Deploy Zhurong rover safely to Utopia Planitia surface
Probe subsurface ice structures using orbital radar
majorDiscoveries: Completed global high-resolution imaging survey of the entire Martian surface
MOSIR subsurface radar mapped layered sedimentary and ice structures in Utopia Planitia
majorAchievements: China's first independent Mars mission achieving orbit, landing, and roving on first attempt
timeline: 2020-07-23: Launched on Long March 5 from Wenchang
2021-02-10: Mars Orbit Insertion
2021-05-14: Zhurong lander/rover successfully landed on Utopia Planitia
2022-06-29: Orbiter completed global coverage survey of Mars
interestingFacts: Tianwen-1 deployed small detachable wireless selfie cameras in deep space to take pictures of itself orbiting Mars.
description: Tianwen-1 is China's first independent Mars exploration mission. It successfully placed an orbiter around Mars while landing the Zhurong rover in Utopia Planitia.

name: BepiColombo
instruments: Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO: BELA laser altimeter, SIMBIO-SYS imager, MERTIS spectrometer)
Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO / Mio: MGF magnetometer, MPPE particle sensor)
missionObjectives: Dual-orbiter investigation of Mercury's composition, geophysics, magnetosphere, and origin
Test general relativity predictions near the Sun's deep gravity well
majorDiscoveries: Captured close-up flyby images of Mercury surface features (Manley crater, volcanic plains)
Conducted joint flybys of Earth, Venus (2 flybys), and Mercury (multiple gravity assists)
majorAchievements: Joint ESA/JAXA mission carrying two independent orbiters inside Mercury Transfer Module (MTM)
timeline: 2018-10-20: Launched on Ariane 5 from Kourou
2020-04-10: Earth flyby
2020-10-15: First Venus flyby
2021-10-01: First Mercury flyby
2026-11-01: Targeted final orbit insertion around Mercury
interestingFacts: Named after Italian mathematician Giuseppe 'Bepi' Colombo, who pioneered the planetary gravity assist technique.
description: BepiColombo is a joint ESA/JAXA dual-orbiter mission en route to Mercury. Comprising ESA's MPO and JAXA's Mio, BepiColombo will map Mercury's magnetosphere and surface composition.
primaryDiscoveries: High-resolution Flyby Imagery of Mercury Craters

name: Lucy Spacecraft
instruments: L'Ralph (Multispectral Imager MVIC & Infrared Spectrometer LEISA)
missionObjectives: Perform first reconnaissance of 10 Jupiter Trojan asteroids across both L4 and L5 swarms
Determine Trojan surface geology, composition, density, and satellite systems
Test Nice model of outer solar system giant planet migration
majorDiscoveries: Discovered unexpected contact binary satellite 'Dinkinesh-Selam' during 2023 test flyby of asteroid 152830 Dinkinesh
Revealed Dinkinesh's moon Selam to be the first known contact binary moon of an asteroid
majorAchievements: First space mission targeting Jupiter's Trojan asteroids
Will visit more independent solar system targets than any previous spacecraft (10 asteroids)
timeline: 2021-10-16: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2023-11-01: Flyby of main belt asteroid 152830 Dinkinesh & discovery of Selam
2025-04-20: Targeted flyby of main belt asteroid 52246 Donaldjohanson
2027-08-12: Arrival at L4 Trojan swarm (Eurybates)
interestingFacts: Named after the famous 'Lucy' fossil hominin, because Trojan asteroids are 'fossils' of planet formation.
description: Lucy is a NASA Discovery program space probe exploring 10 Jupiter Trojan asteroids to study primitive planet-forming materials.

name: Psyche Spacecraft
instruments: DSOC (Deep Space Optical Communications Laser Demonstration)
missionObjectives: Explore metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche, believed to be exposed nickel-iron core of a protoplanet
Determine whether 16 Psyche is a remnant core or unmelted primordial material
Demonstrate high-data-rate Deep Space Optical Communications (DSOC) via laser
majorDiscoveries: Successfully demonstrated deep-space optical laser communication from 16 million km away (DSOC)
En route to Mars gravity assist (2026) and 16 Psyche orbital arrival (2029)
majorAchievements: First space mission dedicated to exploring a metal-world
First deep-space optical laser communication test (DSOC)
timeline: 2023-10-13: Launched on SpaceX Falcon Heavy
2023-11-14: First light success of DSOC laser communication
2026-05-01: Mars gravity assist flyby
2029-08-01: Orbit insertion around 16 Psyche
interestingFacts: Asteroid 16 Psyche is composed largely of metallic nickel-iron, offering humanity a glimpse into planetary cores.
description: Psyche is a NASA space probe en route to explore metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche in the main asteroid belt, while testing laser optical communication across deep space.
primaryDiscoveries: DSOC 16 Million km Laser Data Stream

name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
instruments: OCAMS (OSIRIS-REx Camera Suite: PolyCam, MapCam, SamCam)
missionObjectives: Collect pristine carbonaceous surface sample from near-Earth asteroid 101955 Bennu and return to Earth
Analyze Bennu's organic chemistry, water-bearing minerals, and Yarkovsky effect trajectory nudge
Extended OSIRIS-APEX mission: rendezvous with near-Earth asteroid 99942 Apophis during its 2029 close Earth flyby
majorDiscoveries: Returned 121.6 grams of pristine carbonaceous sample to Earth on September 24, 2023
Discovered water and abundant carbon compounds in returned Bennu samples
Found Bennu to be a loosely bound rubble pile asteroid ejecting small rock particles into space
majorAchievements: First US mission to collect and return a sample from a near-Earth asteroid
Largest pristine asteroid sample ever returned to Earth
timeline: 2016-09-08: Launched on Atlas V
2018-12-03: Arrival at asteroid 101955 Bennu
2020-10-20: Touch-And-Go (TAG) sample collection success
2023-09-24: Sample capsule landed at Utah Test and Training Range
2029-04-13: Extended OSIRIS-APEX mission arrival at asteroid Apophis
interestingFacts: When TAGSAM touched Bennu's surface, the ground behaved like a ball pit, offering almost no resistance and letting the sampling head sink 50 cm into the asteroid.
description: OSIRIS-REx is a NASA sample return mission that successfully collected 121.6g of pristine material from near-Earth asteroid Bennu and delivered it to Earth in 2023, before redirecting to Apophis as OSIRIS-APEX.

name: Hayabusa (MUSES-C)
missionObjectives: Perform touchdown sample collection on S-type near-Earth asteroid 25143 Itokawa
Demonstrate microwave ion engine propulsion for interplanetary travel
Return sample capsule safely to Earth
majorDiscoveries: Returned >1,500 microscopic grains from asteroid Itokawa
Proved S-type asteroids are the source body of ordinary LL chondrite meteorites
Revealed Itokawa to be a low-density rubble-pile asteroid
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to bring asteroid samples back to Earth (June 2010)
First spacecraft to take off from an asteroid surface
timeline: 2003-05-09: Launched on M-V rocket
2005-09-12: Arrival at asteroid Itokawa
2005-11-20: Touchdown and sample attempt on Itokawa
2010-06-13: Re-entry capsule landed at Woomera, Australia
interestingFacts: Despite losing reaction wheels, experiencing fuel leaks, and ion engine failures, JAXA engineers nursed Hayabusa home over 7 years.
description: Hayabusa (MUSES-C) was a JAXA space probe that accomplished the world's first sample return from an asteroid (25143 Itokawa) in 2010.

name: Hayabusa2
missionObjectives: Collect surface and sub-surface samples from C-type carbonaceous asteroid 162173 Ryugu
Deploy impactor (SCI) to blast open artificial crater and access pristine interior material
Return capsule to Earth and continue extended mission to fast-spinning asteroid 1998 KY26
majorDiscoveries: Returned 5.4 grams of pristine black carbonaceous sample from Ryugu in December 2020
Discovered 23 amino acids, water, and primitive organic matter in returned Ryugu samples
Successfully created artificial impact crater on Ryugu using copper kinetic impactor
majorAchievements: First mission to collect sub-surface samples from an asteroid using an explosive kinetic impactor
Deployed multiple mobile rovers (MASCOT, MINERVA-II) on asteroid surface
timeline: 2014-12-03: Launched from Tanegashima
2018-06-27: Arrival at asteroid 162173 Ryugu
2019-04-05: SCI copper impactor fired, creating artificial crater
2020-12-06: Sample capsule landed safely at Woomera, Australia
2031-07-01: Targeted extended mission arrival at asteroid 1998 KY26
interestingFacts: Hayabusa2 carried a 2 kg copper projectile that it shot into Ryugu at 2 km/s to blast open a crater and collect untouched underground rock.
description: Hayabusa2 is a JAXA asteroid sample return space probe. It successfully collected surface and subsurface samples from C-type asteroid Ryugu and delivered them to Earth in 2020.

name: Deep Impact / EPOXI
instruments: Smart Impactor Probe (370 kg copper-weighted impactor)
missionObjectives: Slam a 370 kg copper impactor into nucleus of Comet 9P/Tempel 1 to expose pristine interior ice
Analyze ejecta cloud composition and interior comet structure
Extended EPOXI mission: fly by Comet 103P/Hartley 2 and observe exoplanet transits
majorDiscoveries: Tempel 1 collision revealed comet interior is dusty, porous, and fine-grained with low density
Discovered water ice on surface of comet Tempel 1
EPOXI flyby of Comet Hartley 2 showed active hyperactive dry-ice (CO2) jetting
majorAchievements: First space mission to crash an impactor into a comet nucleus
timeline: 2005-01-12: Launched on Delta II
2005-07-04: Impactor collision with Comet Tempel 1 at 10.2 km/s
2010-11-04: EPOXI flyby of Comet 103P/Hartley 2
2013-09-20: Mission concluded after loss of communication
interestingFacts: The 370 kg impactor hit Comet Tempel 1 at 10.2 km/s (23,000 mph), releasing kinetic energy equivalent to 4.8 tons of TNT.
description: Deep Impact was a NASA space probe designed to study the interior composition of Comet 9P/Tempel 1 by releasing a 370 kg copper impactor to collide with its nucleus.

name: Stardust / NExT
instruments: Aerogel Dust Collector (Stardust Sample Return Capsule)
missionObjectives: Collect cometary dust samples from coma of Comet 81P/Wild 2 using aerogel
Collect interstellar dust grains during heliocentric cruise
Extended NExT mission: fly by Comet Tempel 1 to re-image Deep Impact crater
majorDiscoveries: Returned thousands of cometary dust grains to Earth in January 2006
Discovered high-temperature minerals (like olivine and glycine amino acid) in comet Wild 2, proving inner solar system mixing
NExT re-imaged Deep Impact crater on Tempel 1 in 2011
majorAchievements: First space mission to return samples from a comet to Earth
Utilized ultra-low-density aerogel tile collector
timeline: 1999-02-07: Launched on Delta II
2004-01-02: Closest flyby of Comet Wild 2 (237 km)
2006-01-15: Sample return capsule landed at Utah Test and Training Range
2011-02-14: NExT mission flyby of Comet Tempel 1
2011-03-24: Decommissioned
interestingFacts: Stardust captured comet dust moving at 6.1 km/s using silica aerogel—a synthetic porous material that is 99% air.
description: Stardust was a NASA sample return mission that collected coma dust grains from Comet 81P/Wild 2 in aerogel tiles and returned them safely to Earth in 2006.

name: Rosetta Spacecraft
instruments: OSIRIS (Optical, Spectroscopic, and Infrared Remote Imaging System)
ROSINA (Rosetta Orbiter Spectrometer for Ion and Neutral Analysis)
MIRO (Microwave Instrument for the Rosetta Orbiter)
VIRTIS (Visible and Infrared Thermal Imaging Spectrometer)
missionObjectives: Perform first long-term orbital escort of a comet nucleus (67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko)
Deploy Philae lander onto comet surface
Monitor evolution of comet activity through perihelion passage
majorDiscoveries: ROSINA detected glycine, phosphorus, and organic molecules in 67P's atmosphere
Showed 67P's water deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio is 3x Earth's, proving Earth's oceans did not come solely from Jupiter-family comets
Revealed 67P to be a bi-lobed contact binary ('rubber duck' shape)
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit a comet nucleus (2014–2016)
First soft landing on a comet (Philae lander, Nov 2014)
timeline: 2004-03-02: Launched on Ariane 5 from Kourou
2014-08-06: Arrival at Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko
2014-11-12: Philae lander deployed to comet surface
2015-08-13: Comet 67P perihelion passage observed
2016-09-30: Rosetta controlled touchdown on 67P surface
interestingFacts: Rosetta spent 31 months in deep-space hibernation before waking up automatically via alarm clock on January 20, 2014.
description: Rosetta was a landmark ESA mission that became the first spacecraft to orbit a comet nucleus (67P) and deploy a lander (Philae) onto its surface.

name: Philae Comet Lander
instruments: MUPUS (Multi-Purpose Sensors for Surface & Subsurface Science)
CONSERT (Comet Nucleus Sounding Experiment by Radiowave Transmission)
missionObjectives: Perform world's first soft landing on a comet nucleus
Drill into surface ice and analyze organic chemistry of comet 67P
Perform internal radar tomography of comet interior with Rosetta
majorDiscoveries: Detected 16 organic compounds on comet surface, including 4 never before seen on a comet (methyl isocyanate, acetone, propionaldehyde, acetamide)
MUPUS hammer revealed comet surface is covered in hard ice layer tough as solid rock
majorAchievements: First soft landing on a comet nucleus (November 12, 2014)
timeline: 2004-03-02: Launched attached to Rosetta
2014-11-12: Detached from Rosetta and landed on Agilkia/Abydos site on 67P
2015-06-13: Brief wake-up signal received after battery recharge near perihelion
interestingFacts: Philae's harpoons failed to fire on landing, causing it to bounce twice across the comet before settling in a shaded crevice named Abydos.
description: Philae was the robotic lander deployed by ESA's Rosetta spacecraft that performed the first soft landing on a comet nucleus (67P) on November 12, 2014.
observationCapabilities: Comet Surface In-Situ Drilling & Mass Spectrometry

name: Double Asteroid Redirection Test
instruments: DRACO (Didymos Reconnaissance and Asteroid Camera for Optical navigation)
missionObjectives: Demonstrate planetary defense via kinetic impactor method by crashing into asteroid moon Dimorphos
Measure orbit period change of Dimorphos around Didymos using ground telescopes
Image binary asteroid system up to moment of impact
majorDiscoveries: Successfully crashed into Dimorphos at 6.6 km/s on September 26, 2022
Shortened Dimorphos orbital period by 33 minutes (far exceeding 73-second target)
Proved kinetic impactor technique is viable for defending Earth from asteroid threats
majorAchievements: First full-scale planetary defense technology demonstration in history
LICIACube captured real-time images of impact ejecta plume
timeline: 2021-11-24: Launched on Falcon 9 from Vandenberg
2022-09-11: LICIACube released from DART spacecraft
2022-09-26: Historic impact on Dimorphos at 6.6 km/s
interestingFacts: DART altered Dimorphos's 11.9-hour orbit around Didymos by 33 minutes, reshaping the asteroid moon and blasting off thousands of tons of rock debris.
description: DART was a NASA planetary defense space probe that successfully crashed into asteroid moon Dimorphos at 6.6 km/s in 2022, proving kinetic deflection of dangerous asteroids.

name: Hera Spacecraft
missionObjectives: Perform post-impact detailed reconnaissance of DART collision crater on Dimorphos
Measure mass, density, volume, and internal structure of Dimorphos and Didymos
Deploy two CubeSats (Milani and Juventas) to perform low-frequency radar tomography
majorDiscoveries: En route to Didymos binary system; arrival targeted for late 2026
majorAchievements: ESA's first planetary defense mission
First mission to deploy CubeSats in orbit around a binary asteroid
timeline: 2024-10-07: Launched on Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral
2025-03-01: Mars gravity assist flyby
2026-12-28: Targeted arrival at Didymos/Dimorphos binary system
interestingFacts: Hera will deploy Juventas, a CubeSat carrying the smallest radar ever flown in space, to image the interior of Dimorphos.
description: Hera is an ESA planetary defense space probe launched in 2024 to perform detailed post-impact survey of binary asteroid Dimorphos following NASA's DART collision.

name: Parker Solar Probe
instruments: SWEAP (Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons Investigation)
IS☉IS (Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun)
missionObjectives: Fly directly into the Sun's outer corona to uncover mechanisms heating corona to millions of degrees
Determine source regions and acceleration processes of high-speed solar wind
Trace flow of energy and solar energetic particles
majorDiscoveries: First spacecraft in history to 'touch the Sun', crossing Alfvén critical surface into solar atmosphere on Dec 14, 2021
Discovered S-shaped 'switchbacks' in solar wind magnetic fields where field lines reverse direction violently
Captured first visible light images of Venus's nightside surface beneath dense clouds
majorAchievements: Fastest human-made object in history (achieved speeds over 635,000 km/h / 176 km/s)
Closest approach to the Sun of any spacecraft in history (~6.1 million km / 8.8 solar radii)
timeline: 2018-08-12: Launched on Delta IV Heavy from Cape Canaveral
2018-10-29: Became closest human-made object to the Sun
2021-12-14: Officially entered solar atmosphere / corona for first time
2024-12-24: Closest planned perihelion approach at 6.1 million km
interestingFacts: Parker Solar Probe is protected by a 4.5-inch (11.4 cm) thick carbon-composite heat shield that withstands temperatures of nearly 1,370°C while keeping instruments at 29°C.
description: Parker Solar Probe is a NASA solar spacecraft designed to fly directly into the Sun's outer corona. It holds the record for closest solar approach and fastest human-made object.
observationCapabilities: In-Situ Solar Corona Plasma & Magnetic Field Sensing

name: Solar Orbiter
missionObjectives: Perform high-resolution imaging of the Sun's polar regions from high inclinations
Connect in-situ solar wind measurements to solar surface magnetic structures
Study how solar eruptions and flares drive space weather
majorDiscoveries: Discovered miniature solar flares termed 'campfires' bursting across solar surface
Captured highest-resolution images of the Sun's atmosphere ever taken
Discovered solar wind 'pico-flares' providing continuous energy to solar wind
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to image the Sun's uncharted polar regions from high orbital inclination
timeline: 2020-02-10: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2020-06-15: First perihelion and discovery of solar 'campfires'
2025-03-22: First Venus gravity assist to tilt orbit out of ecliptic plane
interestingFacts: Solar Orbiter uses a heat shield covered in a black calcium phosphate coating derived from charred bone material to withstand 520°C.
description: Solar Orbiter is an ESA/NASA solar space observatory designed to capture the first images of the Sun's polar regions while combining in-situ sensors and high-resolution cameras.

name: Ulysses Spacecraft
instruments: EPAC / GAS (Energetic Particle Composition / Interstellar Gas)
URAP (Unified Radio and Plasma Wave Experiment)
missionObjectives: Perform first in-situ measurements of the heliosphere at high solar latitudes above Sun's poles
Examine 3D structure of solar magnetic field and solar wind speed variations
majorDiscoveries: Proved solar wind from solar poles moves at 750 km/s (twice as fast as equatorial solar wind)
Found solar magnetic field is surprisingly uniform across polar regions without localized magnetic poles
Discovered interstellar dust particles entering the solar system
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit above the Sun's north and south poles (achieved via Jupiter gravity assist)
timeline: 1990-10-06: Deployed by STS-41 Discovery
1992-02-08: Jupiter gravity assist redirected spacecraft into 80° inclined polar solar orbit
1994-06-26: First south polar pass of the Sun
2009-06-30: Mission officially ended
interestingFacts: Ulysses used Jupiter's gravity to swing out of the ecliptic plane into a 80° polar solar orbit.
description: Ulysses was a joint ESA/NASA solar mission that used Jupiter's gravity to enter a high-inclination orbit, mapping the Sun's polar wind and magnetic fields for 18 years.

name: Hinode (SOLAR-B)
missionObjectives: Investigate magnetic field interactions driving solar flares and coronal mass ejections
Measure vector magnetic field in the solar photosphere with sub-arcsecond resolution
majorDiscoveries: Discovered micro-flares and magnetic reconnection jets continuously heating corona
Mapped detailed vector magnetic fields in sunspots and solar active regions
majorAchievements: Over 18 years of continuous high-resolution solar magnetic field observations
timeline: 2006-09-22: Launched from Uchinoura
2006-10-23: First light images from SOT and XRT
interestingFacts: Hinode means 'Sunrise' in Japanese.
description: Hinode (SOLAR-B) is a Japanese JAXA solar space telescope equipped with an optical telescope, EUV spectrometer, and X-ray telescope to observe solar magnetic activity.

name: Yohkoh (SOLAR-A)
missionObjectives: Observe solar flares and high-energy solar phenomena during 22nd solar maximum
Perform full-disk soft X-ray imaging of solar corona
majorDiscoveries: Proved magnetic reconnection is the primary energy release engine behind solar flares
Recorded full 11-year solar cycle X-ray evolution of the corona
majorAchievements: First continuous X-ray movie of the solar cycle
timeline: 1991-08-30: Launched from Uchinoura
2001-12-14: Power loss during total solar eclipse caused loss of attitude control
interestingFacts: Yohkoh means 'Sunbeam' in Japanese.
description: Yohkoh (SOLAR-A) was a Japanese space observatory that mapped solar flares and solar corona X-ray emissions across a full 11-year solar cycle.
observationCapabilities: Full-Disk Soft and Hard X-ray Solar Flare Imaging

name: Transition Region and Coronal Explorer
instruments: Cascaded Quadrant EUV/UV Telescope (0.3m Cassegrain optics)
missionObjectives: Explore fine-scale magnetic field structures in solar transition region and corona
High spatial (1 arcsecond) and temporal (2-second cadence) EUV imaging
majorDiscoveries: Captured revolutionary movies of coronal loops, coronal rain, and micro-flares
Proved coronal heating occurs at the base of coronal loops near the chromosphere
majorAchievements: NASA Small Explorer (SMEX) mission providing over 12 years of ultra-fine EUV solar movies
timeline: 1998-04-02: Launched on Pegasus XL
2010-06-21: Decommissioned after SDO commissioning
interestingFacts: TRACE's images of intricate glowing coronal loops became iconic representations of solar physics.
description: TRACE was a NASA Small Explorer satellite that captured high-resolution EUV images and movies of the Sun's coronal loops and transition region.

name: STEREO-A (Ahead)
instruments: SECCHI (Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation)
IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients)
missionObjectives: Provide 3D stereoscopic imaging of the Sun and coronal mass ejections (CMEs)
Track CME trajectories from Sun to Earth for space weather forecasting
majorDiscoveries: First 3D stereoscopic images and full 360-degree views of the Sun (combined with STEREO-B)
Tracked CME propagation through 3D space directly toward Earth
majorAchievements: First mission to view the entire 360° sphere of the Sun simultaneously
timeline: 2006-10-25: Launched alongside STEREO-B on Delta II
2011-02-06: STEREO-A and STEREO-B reached 180° separation, yielding first 360° image of Sun
2023-08-12: STEREO-A completed first Earth flyby loop after 17 years
interestingFacts: STEREO-A orbits the Sun slightly inside Earth's orbit, allowing it to 'gain' on Earth by about 22 degrees per year.
description: STEREO-A is a NASA solar spacecraft orbiting ahead of Earth to provide 3D stereoscopic imaging of coronal mass ejections.

name: STEREO-B (Behind)
instruments: SECCHI (Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation)
IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients)
missionObjectives: Pair with STEREO-A to provide 3D stereoscopic views of coronal mass ejections
Orbit behind Earth to observe the far side of the Sun
majorDiscoveries: Co-created first 360-degree global map of the Sun in 2011
majorAchievements: First stereoscopic 3D observation pair for solar astrophysics
timeline: 2006-10-25: Launched with STEREO-A
2014-10-01: Communication lost during test before solar conjunction
2016-08-21: Contact briefly re-established, then lost again
2018-10-17: Mission officially terminated
interestingFacts: STEREO-B orbited slightly outside Earth's orbit, falling behind Earth by ~22 degrees per year.
description: STEREO-B was the twin spacecraft to STEREO-A, orbiting behind Earth to provide stereoscopic 3D views of coronal mass ejections.

name: Advanced Composition Explorer
instruments: SWEPAM (Solar Wind Electron, Proton, and Alpha Monitor)
missionObjectives: Measure isotopic and elemental composition of solar wind and cosmic rays at Sun-Earth L1
Provide real-time 15-to-45-minute advance warning of incoming space weather solar storms to NOAA
majorDiscoveries: Provided 27+ years of continuous real-time space weather warning data for Earth's power grids and satellites
Measured isotopic composition of galactic cosmic rays revealing galactic evolution
majorAchievements: Primary real-time space weather warning sentinel stationed at L1 since 1997
timeline: 1997-08-25: Launched on Delta II
1997-12-13: Arrived at L1 halo orbit
interestingFacts: ACE provides space weather forecasters at NOAA with a 15-to-45-minute head start before geomagnetic solar storms hit Earth.
description: ACE is a NASA solar and space weather observatory positioned at Sun-Earth L1 that measures solar wind particles and provides real-time solar storm warnings.
observationCapabilities: Real-Time Solar Wind Particle & Magnetic Sensing
primaryDiscoveries: Continuous 27-Year Real-Time Space Weather Early Warning

name: Wind Spacecraft
missionObjectives: Measure un-perturbed solar wind properties before reaching Earth's magnetosphere
Track radio bursts from solar flares and interplanetary shocks
Provide gamma-ray burst timing in conjunction with cosmic network
majorDiscoveries: Over 30 years of continuous pristine solar wind magnetic and plasma measurements
Detected giant gamma-ray flares from magnetars SGR 1900+14 and SGR 1806-20
majorAchievements: Pioneer mission of NASA's Global Geospace Science (GGS) program, operating over 30 years
timeline: 1994-11-01: Launched on Delta II
2004-05-01: Permanently inserted into Sun-Earth L1 orbit
interestingFacts: Wind carries Russia's KONUS instrument, which has been detecting gamma-ray bursts from deep space for over 30 years.
description: Wind is a NASA heliophysics satellite operating at Sun-Earth L1 to measure un-perturbed solar wind and radio waves.
observationCapabilities: In-Situ Solar Wind Plasma & Magnetic Wave Sensing

name: Deep Space Climate Observatory
instruments: NISTAR (National Institute of Standards and Technology Advanced Radiometer)
missionObjectives: Provide real-time 15-to-45-minute advance warnings of geomagnetic solar storms to NOAA
Capture continuous full-disk color images of the sunlit side of Earth using EPIC camera
majorDiscoveries: Captured viral time-lapse images of the Moon transiting across the sunlit face of Earth
Monitored global ozone, vegetation, cloud height, and climate energy balance
majorAchievements: First operational NOAA space weather monitoring mission stationed at L1
Delivers daily full-disk images of Earth from 1.5 million km away
timeline: 2015-02-11: Launched on SpaceX Falcon 9
2015-06-08: Reached Sun-Earth L1 orbit
2015-07-06: First full-disk image of Earth returned
interestingFacts: DSCOVR was originally conceived in 1998 by Vice President Al Gore as 'Triana' to broadcast a continuous live view of Earth.
description: DSCOVR is a NOAA space weather and Earth observation satellite stationed at Sun-Earth L1. It monitors solar wind storms while taking daily full-disk images of Earth.

name: Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph
instruments: UV Spectrograph & Slit-Jaw Imager (0.19m Cassegrain Telescope)
missionObjectives: Trace flow of energy and plasma through solar chromosphere and transition region into corona
Provide high-cadence UV spectra to understand solar atmosphere heating mechanisms
majorDiscoveries: Discovered low-altitude 'heat bombs' in the solar atmosphere releasing massive energy
Mapped plasma jets feeding high-speed solar wind
majorAchievements: NASA Small Explorer mission operating continuously over 11 years
timeline: 2013-06-27: Launched on Pegasus XL
2013-07-17: First light images released
interestingFacts: IRIS takes a spectrum of the Sun's atmosphere every 1 to 2 seconds, uncovering plasma movement at 300,000 km/h.
description: IRIS is a NASA solar Small Explorer satellite that uses UV spectroscopy to study how energy moves through the Sun's chromosphere and transition region into the corona.

name: Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager
instruments: Nine Cryogenic High-Purity Germanium Detectors with Rotating Modulation Collimators (RMCs)
missionObjectives: Perform high-energy imaging and spectroscopy of solar flares in X-rays and gamma rays (3 keV to 17 MeV)
Explore particle acceleration mechanisms in solar flares
majorDiscoveries: Recorded >75,000 solar flare X-ray events over 16 years
Measured gamma-ray line emission proving flare particle acceleration occurs high in coronal loops
Accurately measured solar oblateness (shape of the Sun)
majorAchievements: First imaging of solar flares in hard X-rays and gamma rays
timeline: 2002-02-05: Launched on Pegasus XL as HESI; renamed RHESSI
2018-04-06: Decommissioned after 16 years of service
2023-04-19: Re-entered Earth atmosphere
interestingFacts: RHESSI recorded over 75,000 solar flares across its 16-year lifetime, from tiny microflares to giant gamma-ray eruptions.
description: RHESSI was a NASA Small Explorer solar space telescope designed to image solar flares in hard X-rays and gamma rays.
observationCapabilities: Hard X-ray & Gamma-ray Rotating Modulation Imaging

name: Aditya-L1
instruments: HEL1OS (High Energy L1 Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer)
Advanced Tri-axial High Resolution Digital Magnetometer
missionObjectives: Observe solar corona dynamics, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar flare origin from Sun-Earth L1
Study chromospheric and coronal heating mechanisms in visible, UV, and X-ray bands
Measure in-situ solar wind plasma and magnetic fields at L1
majorDiscoveries: Successfully inserted into halo orbit around L1 on January 6, 2024
Captured full-disk ultraviolet images of the Sun with SUIT
Recorded dynamics of major solar flares during May 2024 geomagnetic storm
majorAchievements: India's first dedicated space observatory to study the Sun
timeline: 2023-09-02: Launched on PSLV-C57 from Sriharikota
2024-01-06: Successfully inserted into Sun-Earth L1 halo orbit
2024-05-10: Observed massive X-class solar flares during 2024 solar storm
interestingFacts: Aditya means 'Sun' in Sanskrit. It is stationed at L1 to enjoy an uninterrupted, continuous view of the Sun without any eclipses.
description: Aditya-L1 is India's first solar space observatory launched by ISRO. Positioned at Sun-Earth L1, it carries seven payloads to study the solar corona, solar wind, and flares.

name: Landsat 8 (LDCM)
instruments: Operational Land Imager (OLI - 9 spectral bands, 30m resolution)
Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS - 2 thermal bands, 100m resolution)
missionObjectives: Continuously acquire high-quality multi-spectral land surface images of Earth
Monitor global land use, deforestation, agriculture, water resources, and natural disasters
majorDiscoveries: Provided 10+ years of uninterrupted 30-meter global land surface imagery for open access
Tracked global Amazon rainforest loss, polar ice sheet retreat, and urban sprawl
majorAchievements: Maintains 50-year unbroken legacy of Landsat Earth observation program (since 1972)
timeline: 2013-02-11: Launched on Atlas V from Vandenberg
2013-05-30: Operational control handed over from NASA to USGS
interestingFacts: Landsat data is completely free and open to the public, generating billions of dollars in economic value for global agriculture and water management.
description: Landsat 8 is a joint USGS/NASA Earth observation satellite providing 30-meter multi-spectral imagery of Earth's land surfaces and coastal zones.
primaryDiscoveries: Global Deforestation & Ice Sheet Change Mapping

name: Landsat 9
missionObjectives: Replaces aging Landsat 7 to work alongside Landsat 8, reducing global land revisit time to 8 days
Monitor climate change, freshwater resources, forest health, and crop yields
majorDiscoveries: Delivers 14-bit radiometric resolution providing higher sensitivity to subtle land surface changes
majorAchievements: Extends Landsat's 50+ year continuous record of space-based Earth observation into the future
timeline: 2021-09-27: Launched on Atlas V from Vandenberg
2021-10-31: First light imagery released
interestingFacts: Together, Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 repeat coverage of any spot on Earth every 8 days.
description: Landsat 9 is a joint NASA/USGS Earth observation satellite launched in 2021 to continue the uninterrupted 50-year global land imaging record.

name: Terra (EOS AM-1)
instruments: ASTER (Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission & Reflection Radiometer - JAXA)
CERES (Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System)
MOPITT (Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere - CSA)
missionObjectives: Flagship satellite of NASA's Earth Observing System (EOS)
Monitor connections between Earth's atmosphere, land, snow/ice, and oceans
Track global wildfire activity, air pollution, cloud cover, and surface temperature
majorDiscoveries: Provided 25 years of daily global wildfire and thermal anomaly mapping via MODIS
Mapped global carbon monoxide pollution transport across continents via MOPITT
Created high-resolution ASTER Global Digital Elevation Model (GDEM)
majorAchievements: Flagship of Earth Observing System operating continuously for over 25 years
timeline: 1999-12-18: Launched on Atlas IIAS from Vandenberg
2000-02-24: Science data collection commenced
interestingFacts: Terra's MODIS camera images almost the entire surface of Earth every one to two days in 36 spectral bands.
description: Terra (EOS AM-1) is the flagship satellite of NASA's Earth Observing System. It carries five multi-national instruments monitoring global climate, wildfires, and atmosphere health.

name: Aqua (EOS PM-1)
instruments: CERES (Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System)
missionObjectives: Study Earth's water cycle: evaporation, atmospheric water vapor, snow cover, sea ice, and ocean temperature
Lead the international afternoon satellite constellation ('A-Train')
majorDiscoveries: Over 22 years of continuous sea ice extent mapping in Arctic and Antarctic
AIRS high-resolution temperature and humidity soundings revolutionized weather forecasting models
majorAchievements: Pioneered the 'A-Train' satellite constellation, flying in tight formation with CALIPSO, CloudSat, and Aura
timeline: 2002-05-04: Launched on Delta II from Vandenberg
2002-06-24: First MODIS Aqua images released
interestingFacts: Aqua was named for the Latin word for water because its instruments focus on all forms of water in Earth's climate.
description: Aqua (EOS PM-1) is a NASA Earth science satellite dedicated to studying Earth's global water cycle, sea ice, cloud cover, and sea surface temperatures.
observationCapabilities: Global Sea Ice & Water Vapor Sounding
primaryDiscoveries: 22+ Year Arctic Sea Ice Decay Mapping

name: Aura (EOS CHEM-1)
missionObjectives: Study Earth's ozone layer health, recovery, and atmospheric chemistry
Monitor air quality, tropospheric pollution, and greenhouse gas trends
majorDiscoveries: Documented recovery of Antarctic ozone hole following Montreal Protocol restrictions
Mapped global nitrogen dioxide (NO2) air pollution trends from urban power plants and traffic
majorAchievements: Over 20 years of continuous global atmospheric chemistry and ozone hole monitoring
timeline: 2004-07-15: Launched on Delta II from Vandenberg
2004-10-01: OMI instrument operational
interestingFacts: Aura's OMI instrument tracked the dramatic drop in nitrogen dioxide pollution over global cities during 2020 lockdowns.
description: Aura (EOS CHEM-1) is a NASA Earth science satellite measuring Earth's ozone layer, air quality, and atmospheric trace gases.
observationCapabilities: Global UV/Vis Ozone & NO2 Air Pollution Spectrometry

name: ICESat-2
launchVehicle: Delta II 7420-10C (Final Flight of Delta II)
instruments: ATLAS (Advanced Topographic Laser Altimeter System - 6 green laser beams)
missionObjectives: Measure polar ice sheet elevation changes in Greenland and Antarctica to 4 millimeter precision
Track sea ice thickness, forest canopy height, and global ocean topography
majorDiscoveries: Mapped annual loss of 318 gigatons of ice per year from Greenland and Antarctica combined
Measured sea ice freeboard and thickness across Arctic Ocean year-round
majorAchievements: Fires 10,000 laser pulses per second across 6 green beams, measuring elevation every 70 cm along track
Final payload launched aboard the historical Delta II rocket
timeline: 2018-09-15: Launched on final Delta II rocket from Vandenberg
2018-10-17: ATLAS green laser turned on; first light measurements
interestingFacts: ICESat-2 fires its green laser 10,000 times a second. If a person were standing under it, they would see a tiny faint green spot flash by on the ground.
description: ICESat-2 is a NASA Earth observation satellite that uses a 6-beam green laser altimeter (ATLAS) to measure ice sheet elevation and sea ice thickness with millimeter accuracy.
primaryDiscoveries: 318 Gigaton Annual Polar Ice Mass Loss Measurement

name: GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO)
missionObjectives: Track global mass movements of water, ice, and groundwater by measuring monthly changes in Earth's gravity field
Measure inter-satellite distance variations to nanometer precision using laser interferometry
majorDiscoveries: Tracked severe groundwater depletion in global aquifers (California Central Valley, India, Middle East)
Measured monthly ice sheet loss rates in Greenland and Antarctica
majorAchievements: Demonstrated sub-micrometer inter-satellite Laser Ranging Interferometry (LRI) in space
timeline: 2018-05-22: Launched on Falcon 9 alongside Iridium NEXT satellites
2018-06-25: Laser Ranging Interferometer (LRI) first light success
interestingFacts: GRACE-FO's two identical satellites fly ~220 km apart, measuring tiny changes in distance between them caused by Earth's gravity pulling on the lead satellite first.
description: GRACE-FO is a joint NASA/GFZ twin-satellite mission that tracks monthly shifts in Earth's gravity field to monitor groundwater loss and ice melt.

name: Soil Moisture Active Passive
missionObjectives: Map top 5 cm surface soil moisture globally every 2–3 days
Determine freeze/thaw state in high-latitude boreal regions to monitor carbon cycle
majorDiscoveries: Created global high-resolution soil moisture maps improving drought monitoring and flood forecasting
Monitored sea surface salinity and hurricane wind speeds
majorAchievements: Features 6-meter lightweight mesh reflector antenna spinning at 14.6 RPM
timeline: 2015-01-31: Launched on Delta II from Vandenberg
2015-04-30: Radar amplifier failed; radiometer continues full science
interestingFacts: SMAP's gold-plated 6-meter mesh dish unfurled in space like a giant spinning lasso.
description: SMAP is a NASA Earth science satellite equipped with a 6-meter rotating mesh antenna to measure global soil moisture and freeze/thaw cycles.
observationCapabilities: 6-Meter Spinning Mesh Reflector L-band Microwave Sensing

name: Surface Water and Ocean Topography
missionObjectives: First global survey of Earth's surface water in 3D: lakes, rivers, reservoirs, and ocean eddies
Measure ocean topography at 10-times finer spatial resolution than previous altimeters
majorDiscoveries: Mapped 3D water elevations for over 6 million lakes and rivers worldwide
Resolved small-scale ocean eddies and currents that absorb atmospheric heat and carbon
majorAchievements: First wide-swath radar interferometric satellite for hydrology
timeline: 2022-12-16: Launched on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg
2023-01-20: KaRIn radar antennas deployed successfully
interestingFacts: SWOT uses a 10-meter boom carrying radar antennas at each end to measure water height across a 120-km wide swath.
description: SWOT is an international satellite mission led by NASA and CNES that surveys Earth's surface water in 3D, measuring lake, river, and ocean heights with wide-swath radar.
primaryDiscoveries: Global 3D Mapping of 6 Million Lakes & Rivers

name: Sentinel-2A
missionObjectives: Provide free, open high-resolution optical imaging for Copernicus land monitoring
Monitor vegetation, agriculture, forest cover, inland water, and coastal zones
majorDiscoveries: Delivers 10-meter resolution images every 5 days globally (combined with Sentinel-2B)
Widely used for agriculture monitoring, disaster response, and environmental protection
majorAchievements: Core optical land mission of the European Union's Copernicus program
timeline: 2015-06-23: Launched on Vega from Kourou
2015-06-27: First light image of Italy and the Alps returned
interestingFacts: Sentinel-2 uses a laser link (EDRS) to transmit massive image data to geostationary satellites for real-time delivery to ground stations.
description: Sentinel-2A is an ESA multi-spectral Earth observation satellite operating under the Copernicus program, delivering free 10-meter optical images for global land monitoring.

name: Sentinel-1A
missionObjectives: Provide day-and-night, all-weather C-band radar imaging of Earth land and sea surface
Monitor sea ice extent, oil spills, earthquake land displacements, and flood mapping
majorDiscoveries: Mapped radar ground displacements from major earthquakes (Turkey, Nepal, Italy) to millimeter accuracy via interferometry (InSAR)
Monitored shipping routes, iceberg calving, and forest logging day and night
majorAchievements: First satellite launched for the EU's flagship Copernicus program
timeline: 2014-04-03: Launched on Soyuz from Kourou
2014-04-12: First radar image of Brussels returned
interestingFacts: Sentinel-1 uses synthetic aperture radar to see through dense clouds, rain, and total darkness.
description: Sentinel-1A is an ESA C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite providing all-weather day-and-night imaging under the Copernicus program.
observationCapabilities: C-band All-Weather Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging
primaryDiscoveries: InSAR Millimeter Earthquake Ground Displacement Mapping

name: Sentinel-5 Precursor (Sentinel-5P)
missionObjectives: Monitor air quality, trace gas emissions (NO2, methane, SO2, CO, ozone, formaldehyde), and aerosols globally every day
Pinpoint industrial methane leaks and greenhouse gas sources
majorDiscoveries: Mapped major global industrial methane leaks from pipelines, oil fields, and landfills
Monitored global air pollution reductions during 2020 lockdowns with unprecedented 3.5×5.5 km resolution
majorAchievements: Highest spatial resolution air quality spectrometer in orbit (TROPOMI)
timeline: 2017-10-13: Launched on Rockot from Plesetsk
2017-12-01: First TROPOMI global air pollution maps released
interestingFacts: TROPOMI on Sentinel-5P scans a 2,600 km wide strip of Earth every day, measuring air pollution in cities down to neighborhood scales.
description: Sentinel-5P is an ESA Copernicus satellite carrying TROPOMI, the world's most advanced air pollution spectrometer, to track methane leaks and urban emissions daily.
observationCapabilities: TROPOMI 3.5x5.5 km Daily Global Air Quality Spectrometry

name: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR)
missionObjectives: Perform dual-frequency (L-band and S-band) SAR radar mapping of Earth's land and ice surfaces every 12 days
Measure millimeter-scale land deformations from earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides, and ice sheet movement
Map global forest biomass, wetland ecosystems, and agricultural crop growth
majorDiscoveries: Targeted for launch in mid-2025
majorAchievements: First dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar satellite; carries largest deployable reflector antenna deployed by NASA (12 meters)
timeline: 2023-03-08: NASA L-band radar delivered to ISRO in Bengaluru
2025-06-01: Targeted launch window aboard GSLV Mk II
interestingFacts: NISAR will scan almost the entire land and ice surface of Earth every 12 days, measuring ground movements down to fractions of an inch.
description: NISAR is a landmark joint NASA-ISRO satellite mission featuring dual L-band and S-band radar to map Earth's land surface deformations, ice sheet movement, and forest biomass.
primaryDiscoveries: Targeted Global 12-Day Millimeter Ground Deformation Map

name: International Space Station
manufacturer: Boeing / RSC Energia / Thales Alenia / Mitsubishi
instruments: EMIT (Earth Surface Mineral Dust Source Investigation)
missionObjectives: Provide long-duration microgravity research laboratory for human physiology, material science, and biology
Maintain continuous human presence in space since November 2, 2000
Serve as testbed for deep-space technologies and human exploration of the Moon and Mars
majorDiscoveries: AMS-02 detected over 200 billion cosmic ray events, shedding light on dark matter signatures and antimatter
Proved human body adaptation mechanisms and long-duration bone density loss countermeasures (NASA Twin Study)
Demonstrated capillary flow, cold atom lab quantum condensate production, and protein crystal growth
majorAchievements: Continuous human occupancy for over 25 consecutive years
Largest single structure ever assembled in space (109m x 73m)
timeline: 1998-11-20: Zarya functional cargo block launched from Baikonur
2000-11-02: Expedition 1 crew arrived (William Shepherd, Sergei Krikalev, Yuri Gidzenko)
2011-05-16: AMS-02 cosmic ray detector installed
2020-05-31: SpaceX Crew Dragon Demo-2 docked, launching commercial crew era
interestingFacts: The ISS travels at 28,000 km/h (7.66 km/s), orbiting Earth every 90 minutes. Astronauts aboard witness 16 sunrises and sunsets every single day.
description: The International Space Station (ISS) is a state-of-the-art modular space station orbiting Earth. Jointly operated by NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, and CSA, it has been continuously inhabited since November 2000.
primaryDiscoveries: Human Bone Density Loss Prevention Protocols

name: Mir Space Station
missionObjectives: Operate world's first continuously inhabited modular research space station
Test long-duration human spaceflight physiology and station assembly techniques
Shuttle-Mir program: foster post-Cold War US-Russian space cooperation
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated human body survivability for over one full year in microgravity (Valeri Polyakov set 437-day record)
Pioneered modular space assembly and multi-national crew station operations
majorAchievements: World's first modular space station assembled in orbit
Valeri Polyakov completed longest single spaceflight in human history (437 days, 18 hours)
timeline: 1986-02-20: Mir core module launched from Baikonur
1995-03-22: Valeri Polyakov returned to Earth after 437 days aboard Mir
1995-06-29: STS-71 Space Shuttle Atlantis docked with Mir for first time
2001-03-23: Controlled atmospheric re-entry into South Pacific Ocean
interestingFacts: Mir means 'Peace' or 'World' in Russian. It hosted 125 cosmonauts and astronauts from 12 countries over 15 years.
description: Mir was the world's first modular space station, launched by the Soviet Union in 1986. It hosted record-breaking long-duration crews and paved the way for the ISS through the Shuttle-Mir Program.
observationCapabilities: Modular Space Station Habitat & X-ray Astrophysics Module

name: Skylab Space Station
missionObjectives: America's first orbital space station to prove humans can live and work productively in space
Perform solar astronomy using Apollo Telescope Mount (ATM) outside Earth's atmosphere
Study Earth resources and human endurance across 28-day, 59-day, and 84-day missions
majorDiscoveries: Atmospheric solar images from Apollo Telescope Mount discovered solar coronal holes
Proved human crew can perform complex orbital repairs (erected parasol heat shield and un-jammed solar wing)
majorAchievements: America's first space station
Skylab 4 crew set human spaceflight duration record of 84 days in 1974
timeline: 1973-05-14: Uncrewed Skylab station launched on final Saturn V rocket
1973-05-25: Skylab 2 crew arrived and repaired damaged thermal shield and solar array
1974-02-08: Skylab 4 crew departed after 84 days
1979-07-11: Atmospheric re-entry over Indian Ocean and Western Australia
interestingFacts: Skylab was built inside a modified Saturn V upper stage (S-IVB), providing a living volume as large as a 3-bedroom house.
description: Skylab was the United States' first space station, launched by NASA in 1973. Constructed from a converted Saturn V upper stage, it featured the Apollo Telescope Mount for solar observation.
observationCapabilities: Apollo Telescope Mount Solar X-Ray/UV Imaging

name: Salyut 7 Space Station
missionObjectives: Conduct long-duration crewed orbital science, microgravity metallurgy, and Earth observation
Test heavy TKS module docking and orbital space station servicing
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated total dead-station orbital rescue in 1985 (Soyuz T-13 mission by Dzhanibekov and Savinykh)
Set continuous space duration record of 237 days in 1984
majorAchievements: Final space station of the Soviet Salyut program
Pioneered heroic manual docking to an unpowered, tumbling space station
timeline: 1982-04-19: Launched on Proton-K from Baikonur
1985-06-06: Soyuz T-13 legendary rescue mission docked with frozen dead station
1986-05-05: Soyuz T-15 crew performed first space-station-to-space-station transfer (Salyut 7 to Mir)
1991-02-07: Atmospheric re-entry over Argentina
interestingFacts: Cosmonauts Vladimir Dzhanibekov and Viktor Savinykh docked manually with dead Salyut 7 in total darkness, thawed the frozen ice-covered interior, and restored full power.
description: Salyut 7 was the final space station of the Soviet Salyut program. Operational from 1982 to 1991, it became famous for the legendary 1985 rescue mission by Soyuz T-13.

name: Tiangong Space Station (China Space Station)
launchVehicle: Long March 5B / Long March 2F / Long March 7
missionObjectives: Operate China's long-term modular space station with 3-person permanent crew rotations
Conduct international microgravity biology, fluid physics, combustion, and space astronomy research
Co-orbit with Xuntian Space Station Telescope (CSST)

Conducted space science lectures ('Tiangong Classrooms') and long-duration microgravity biological experiments

Achieved seamless crew handovers in orbit with up to 6 taikonauts aboard
timeline: 2021-04-29: Tianhe core module launched on Long March 5B
2021-06-17: Shenzhou-12 crew arrived (first taikonauts aboard)
2022-07-24: Wentian lab module docked
2022-10-31: Mengtian lab module docked, completing basic T-shape structure
interestingFacts: Tiangong means 'Heavenly Palace' in Chinese. The station features a state-of-the-art cold atom physics rack capable of producing quantum Bose-Einstein Condensates in microgravity.
description: Tiangong is China's modular space station in low Earth orbit. Assembled between 2021 and 2022, it consists of the Tianhe core module and Wentian and Mengtian science laboratories.
observationCapabilities: Permanent Taikonaut Habitat & Cold Atom Physics Laboratory

name: Gateway (Lunar Gateway Space Station)
manufacturer: Maxar Technologies / Northrop Grumman / Thales Alenia
instruments: Power and Propulsion Element (PPE - 60kW Solar Electric Propulsion)
HERMES (Heliophysics Environmental and Radiation Measurement Experiment)

Perform deep-space radiation research outside Earth's protective magnetosphere
Serve as staging location for future crewed missions to Mars
majorDiscoveries: PPE and HALO modules targeted for co-manifested launch aboard SpaceX Falcon Heavy
majorAchievements: First international crewed space station built in lunar orbit
timeline: 2027-12-01: Targeted co-manifested launch of PPE and HALO aboard Falcon Heavy
Targeted arrival into Lunar Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO)

description: Gateway is an international crewed space station planned for assembly in lunar orbit under NASA's Artemis program. Positioned in a Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit, Gateway will serve as a staging post for lunar landings and Mars missions.
observationCapabilities: 60kW Solar Electric Propulsion & Deep-Space Radiation Monitoring
primaryDiscoveries: Targeted 2027 First Lunar Orbit Station Assembly

name: Soyuz Crewed Spacecraft Fleet (Soyuz TMA / MS)
missionObjectives: Provide long-running, reliable human space transport and lifeboat services to space stations
Transport cosmonauts and international astronauts to Salyut, Mir, and ISS
majorDiscoveries: Over 150 successful crewed spaceflights completed since 1967
Served as the sole crew transport vehicle to the ISS for nearly 9 years (2011–2020) following Space Shuttle retirement
majorAchievements: Longest-running human spaceflight vehicle program in space history (>57 years)
timeline: 1967-04-23: Soyuz 1 maiden crewed flight
1975-07-15: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project historic docking
2000-10-31: Soyuz TM-31 launched Expedition 1 crew to ISS
2020-04-09: Soyuz MS-16 launched during COVID-19 pandemic
interestingFacts: Soyuz is divided into three modules: the spherical Orbital Module, the bell-shaped Descent Module, and the Service Module. Only the middle Descent Module returns to Earth.
description: Soyuz is Russia's legendary crewed spacecraft series, operating continuously since 1967. Over 150 crewed missions have transported cosmonauts and astronauts to Salyut, Mir, and the ISS.
observationCapabilities: Kurs-NA Automated Radar Docking & Soft Terrestrial Parachute Landing
primaryDiscoveries: 57+ Years Continuous Crew Spaceflight Operational Record

name: Apollo 11 Mission
missionObjectives: Perform first crewed lunar landing and return safely to Earth
Explore lunar surface at Sea of Tranquility and collect lunar rock/soil samples
Deploy scientific experiments and laser retroreflector on Moon surface
majorDiscoveries: Returned 21.55 kg of pristine lunar rocks (basalts and breccias), proving Moon formed via high-temperature magmatic processes
Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR) is still active today, measuring Earth-Moon distance to millimeter precision
majorAchievements: First human landing on the Moon (Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, July 20, 1969)
Historic milestone fulfillling President John F. Kennedy's 1961 goal
timeline: 1969-07-16: Launched on Saturn V from Kennedy Space Center
1969-07-20 20:17 UTC: Lunar Module Eagle landed at Sea of Tranquility
1969-07-21 02:56 UTC: Neil Armstrong stepped onto Moon: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind'
1969-07-24: Splashdown in North Pacific Ocean; recovered by USS Hornet
interestingFacts: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent 21 hours and 36 minutes on the lunar surface, taking 2 hours and 31 minutes of moonwalk EVAs.
description: Apollo 11 was the historic NASA spaceflight that landed the first two humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Commander Neil Armstrong and Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin walked on the lunar surface while Command Module Pilot Michael Collins orbited above.

name: Apollo 13 Mission
instruments: Lunar Module Aquarius Life Support Systems
missionObjectives: Perform third crewed lunar landing at Fra Mauro highlands (aborted due to oxygen tank explosion)
Return crew safely to Earth using Lunar Module Aquarius as a 'lifeboat'
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated extraordinary mission control crisis management and engineering adaptability under extreme conditions
majorAchievements: Set human altitude record for farthest distance from Earth ever reached by humans (400,171 km)
Successful rescue of Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise following major explosion in space
timeline: 1970-04-11: Launched on Saturn V from Kennedy Space Center
1970-04-13 55:54 GET: Oxygen tank #2 exploded: 'Houston, we've had a problem here'
1970-04-14: Trajectory corrected using LM descent engine to free-return trajectory around Moon
1970-04-17: Safe splashdown in South Pacific Ocean
interestingFacts: During their looping flyby around the far side of the Moon, the Apollo 13 crew reached 400,171 km from Earth—a record for farthest human space travel that stands to this day.
description: Apollo 13 was NASA's third intended lunar landing mission. An oxygen tank explosion 56 hours after launch disabled the Service Module, forcing crew members Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise to use Lunar Module Aquarius as a lifeboat to return safely to Earth.

name: Space Shuttle Orbiter Fleet (Discovery, Atlantis, Endeavour, Columbia, Challenger)
missionObjectives: Provide world's first reusable winged spacecraft for crew and heavy payload transport to low Earth orbit
Deploy, repair, and service space telescopes (Hubble Space Telescope)
Assemble International Space Station (ISS) and Mir modules
majorDiscoveries: Repaired and upgraded Hubble Space Telescope across 5 servicing missions
SRTM radar mapped 80% of Earth's land surface topography in 3D in 11 days (2000)
Delivered over 1.3 million kg of cargo and 355 individuals into space
majorAchievements: 135 total space missions completed over 30 years of winged spaceflight (1981–2011)
Assembled the International Space Station in orbit
timeline: 1981-04-12: STS-1 historic first orbital flight of Columbia (John Young, Bob Crippen)
1990-04-24: STS-31 deployed Hubble Space Telescope
1993-12-02: STS-61 first Hubble servicing mission
2011-07-21: STS-135 final landing of Atlantis, concluding Shuttle program
interestingFacts: The Space Shuttle re-entered Earth's atmosphere at Mach 25 (27,000 km/h), protected by over 24,000 individual silica heat shield tiles.
description: NASA's Space Shuttle was the world's first reusable winged crewed spaceplane. Operating across 135 missions between 1981 and 2011, the fleet deployed satellites, serviced Hubble, and assembled the ISS.
observationCapabilities: Winged Atmospheric Re-entry Glider & Payload Bay Deployment

name: SpaceX Crew Dragon (Dragon 2)
missionObjectives: Provide safe, reliable commercial crew transport for 4–7 astronauts to and from the ISS
Perform private commercial research missions in Earth orbit (Inspiration4, Polaris Dawn, Axiom missions)
Conduct historic extravehicular activities (EVA) from commercial spacecraft
majorDiscoveries: Polaris Dawn mission executed world's first commercial spacewalk (EVA) on September 12, 2024
Inspiration4 executed world's first all-civilian orbital spaceflight in September 2021
majorAchievements: First privately developed crewed spacecraft to launch humans into orbit and dock with the ISS
Restored American human spaceflight capability from US soil in 2020
timeline: 2020-05-30: Demo-2 launch carrying Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken (first crewed flight)
2020-05-31: Autonomous docking with the ISS
2021-09-15: Inspiration4 all-civilian orbital mission
2024-09-12: Polaris Dawn commercial spacewalk executed
interestingFacts: Crew Dragon features 8 SuperDraco engines built into its side walls capable of launching the capsule away from an exploding rocket in 1/10th of a second.
description: Crew Dragon (Dragon 2) is a reusable commercial spacecraft developed by SpaceX under NASA's Commercial Crew Program. It routinely carries astronauts and private crews to the ISS.
observationCapabilities: Autonomous Laser IDSS Docking & SuperDraco Launch Abort

name: Artemis I Mission
manufacturer: Lockheed Martin / Boeing / Aerojet Rocketdyne / Northrop Grumman
instruments: Helga and Zohar Radiation Phantom Torso Sensors
10 CubeSat Secondary Payloads (BioSentinel, Lunar IceCube, CAPSTONE)
missionObjectives: Perform integrated uncrewed flight test of Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft around the Moon
Test Orion's heat shield during 40,000 km/h Earth atmospheric re-entry
Validate deep-space operations in Lunar Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO)
majorDiscoveries: Proved Orion heat shield and life-support radiation protection systems perform within strict human rating specs
Traveled farther from Earth than any human-rated spacecraft in history (432,210 km)
majorAchievements: Maiden flight of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS), the most powerful operational rocket ever launched at ignition (8.8 million lbs thrust)
timeline: 2022-11-16: Night launch on SLS Block 1 from Kennedy Space Center
2022-11-21: Closest flyby of Moon surface (130 km)
2022-11-25: Entered Lunar Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO)
2022-12-11: Skip re-entry and splashdown in Pacific Ocean
interestingFacts: Orion broke Apollo 13's record for the farthest distance traveled by a human-rated spacecraft, flying 432,210 km from Earth.
description: Artemis I was the uncrewed inaugural flight test of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft. Orion orbited the Moon in Distant Retrograde Orbit before executing a precision Pacific splashdown.
observationCapabilities: Skip Re-entry Atmospheric Thermal Protection Test
primaryDiscoveries: Orion Deep Space Human Rating Certification

name: Artemis II Mission
missionObjectives: First crewed flight of NASA's Artemis program, taking 4 astronauts around the Moon
Test Orion spacecraft life support, manual proximity maneuvering, and communication systems with humans aboard
Perform free-return lunar flyby taking crew 10,000 km beyond the lunar far side
majorDiscoveries: En route for crewed lunar flyby with Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen
majorAchievements: First humans to travel to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972
First Canadian astronaut (Jeremy Hansen) and first woman/person of color to travel to lunar orbit
timeline: 2026-04-01: Targeted launch on SLS Block 1 from Kennedy Space Center
Lunar free-return flyby 10,000 km above lunar far side
Precision splashdown in Pacific Ocean
interestingFacts: Artemis II astronaut Christina Koch will become the first woman to travel to the Moon, while Jeremy Hansen will become the first non-American to fly into deep space.
description: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission under the Artemis program. Carrying four astronauts (Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen), Orion will perform a 10-day free-return flyby around the Moon.
observationCapabilities: Optical Laser O2O Deep Space Data Transfer

name: Shenzhou Crewed Spacecraft Series
missionObjectives: Provide independent human spaceflight capability for 3-person taikonaut crews
Transport crews and high-priority cargo to and from Tiangong Space Station

Routine 6-month crew rotations to Tiangong Space Station
majorAchievements: Over 18 successful crewed and uncrewed spaceflight missions since 1999

2003-10-15: Shenzhou 5 launched Yang Liwei (China's first human in space)
2008-09-27: Shenzhou 7 executed China's first spacewalk (Zhai Zhigang)
2021-06-17: Shenzhou 12 docked with Tiangong Space Station core module
interestingFacts: Shenzhou means 'Divine Vessel' or 'Divine Craft' in Chinese.
description: Shenzhou is China's family of crewed spacecraft. Operating since 1999, Shenzhou spacecraft carry up to three taikonauts to low Earth orbit and the Tiangong Space Station.
observationCapabilities: Autonomous Proximity Rendezvous & Parachute Terrestrial Landing

name: Orion Multi-Purpose Crew Vehicle (MPCV)
launchVehicle: Delta IV Heavy / Space Launch System (SLS)
manufacturer: Lockheed Martin / Airbus Defence and Space
instruments: Crew Module (CM - 4-person deep space life support)
European Service Module (ESM - Airbus main engine & 4 solar wings)

Withstand 40,000 km/h lunar re-entry heat speeds (11.2 km/s)
Provide long-duration life support outside Earth's magnetosphere

Proved European Service Module (ESM) solar electric and propulsion systems in deep space
majorAchievements: NASA's primary deep-space crew capsule for Artemis lunar exploration
timeline: 2014-12-05: EFT-1 inaugural uncrewed orbital flight test on Delta IV Heavy
2022-11-16: Artemis I lunar orbit launch
2026-04-01: Targeted Artemis II crewed lunar flyby
interestingFacts: Orion's heat shield is 5 meters (16.5 ft) in diameter, making it the largest heat shield ever built. It withstands temperatures near 2,800°C during lunar re-entry.
description: Orion (MPCV) is NASA's flagship deep-space crewed capsule built by Lockheed Martin and Airbus. Designed to transport four astronauts to the Moon and Gateway, Orion withstands high-speed lunar re-entry speeds.
observationCapabilities: 11.2 km/s Lunar Atmospheric Re-entry Skip Maneuver

name: SpaceX Starship Human Landing System (Starship HLS)
missionType: Crewed Lunar Lander / Reusable Super-Heavy Spacecraft

In-Space Cryogenic Liquid Oxygen / Methane Transfer System

Demonstrate orbital cryogenic propellant transfer in low Earth orbit
Provide fully reusable super-heavy launch system capable of placing 100+ tons of payload into orbit

Integrated Starship flight test 5 (October 2024) achieved historic 'Mechazilla' launch tower chopsticks catch of Super Heavy booster
majorAchievements: Selected by NASA as the human lander for Artemis III and Artemis IV missions
Largest and most powerful launch vehicle ever flown in human history (16.7 million lbs thrust at launch)
timeline: 2023-04-20: Integrated Flight Test 1 (IFT-1) maiden launch from Starbase
2024-06-06: IFT-4 completed controlled re-entry and ocean touchdown
2024-10-13: IFT-5 historic booster catch by Mechazilla launch tower
2027-09-01: Targeted Artemis III crewed lunar landing at South Pole
interestingFacts: Starship stands 121 meters (397 ft) tall—taller than a 35-story building and produces double the thrust of the historic Saturn V rocket.
description: Starship HLS is the crewed lunar landing variant of SpaceX's fully reusable Starship system. Selected by NASA for the Artemis III mission, Starship HLS will land astronauts near the Moon's South Pole.
observationCapabilities: Autonomous LIDAR South Pole Lunar Precision Landing
primaryDiscoveries: First Launch Tower Booster Chopsticks Catch (2024)

name: Global Positioning System (GPS / NAVSTAR)
missionObjectives: Provide continuous 24/7 global position, velocity, and precise timing signals anywhere on Earth
Support global aviation, maritime navigation, mobile telecommunications, financial networks, and military operations

timeline: 1978-02-22: First NAVSTAR GPS Block I satellite launched
1995-07-17: GPS achieved Full Operational Capability (FOC)
2018-12-23: First GPS III next-generation satellite launched on Falcon 9
interestingFacts: Without relativistic corrections, GPS receivers would accumulate errors of over 10 km every day because atomic clocks run 38 microseconds faster per day in orbit than on Earth.
description: GPS (NAVSTAR) is a US Space Force space-based radionavigation satellite constellation providing continuous 3D positioning, navigation, and precise timing worldwide.
observationCapabilities: Continuous Global Atomic Time & Position Signal Broadcast
primaryDiscoveries: Gravitational Time Dilation 38 μs/day Empirical Proof

name: Galileo Navigation Satellite System
partnerAgencies: European Union Agency for the Space Programme (EUSPA)
instruments: Passive Hydrogen Maser (PHM - 1 sec drift in 3 million years)

Deliver sub-meter positioning accuracy for civilian devices globally
Provide real-time distress beacon tracking via Cospas-Sarsat Search and Rescue (SAR)

Search and Rescue (SAR) service reduced emergency beacon distress location times from hours to 10 minutes
majorAchievements: Europe's flagship global navigation satellite system (28 active operational satellites)
timeline: 2011-10-21: First operational IOV satellites launched on Soyuz from Kourou
2016-12-15: Galileo Initial Services officially declared operational
2024-04-28: First Galileo satellites launched on SpaceX Falcon 9
interestingFacts: Galileo satellites carry Passive Hydrogen Maser atomic clocks that lose less than 1 second every 3 million years.
description: Galileo is the European Union's civilian global navigation satellite system. Built by ESA and operated by EUSPA, Galileo delivers sub-meter positioning precision worldwide.
observationCapabilities: Passive Hydrogen Maser Atomic Timekeeping & Search & Rescue Transponder

name: Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRSS)
missionObjectives: Provide continuous 100% orbital communication coverage for NASA spacecraft (ISS, Hubble, Landsat) in low Earth orbit
Eliminate reliance on ground tracking stations around the world
majorDiscoveries: Enabled continuous live HD video streaming and high-speed data transmission from the International Space Station and Space Shuttle
majorAchievements: NASA's primary space backbone communications network for over 40 years (13 TDRS satellites launched)
timeline: 1983-04-04: TDRS-1 deployed by STS-6 Space Shuttle Challenger
2017-08-18: TDRS-13 (final 3rd generation satellite) launched on Atlas V
interestingFacts: Before TDRS, NASA spacecraft lost communication during 85% of their orbit because they could only talk to ground stations when directly overhead.
description: TDRSS is NASA's constellation of geostationary communications relay satellites. TDRS satellites provide continuous high-speed data relay for the ISS, Hubble Space Telescope, and Earth-observing satellites.

name: Boeing X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle (OTV)
orbitType: Low Earth Orbit / Highly Elliptical Orbit
instruments: PRAM (Photovoltaic Radiofrequency Antenna Module - Space Solar Power Test)
METTS (NASA Materials Exposure in Space Payload)
missionObjectives: Demonstrate reusable uncrewed spaceplane technologies: heat shields, autonomous re-entry, and landing
Perform long-duration orbital technology experiments for US Space Force and NASA

OTV-6 mission spent 908 consecutive days in orbit before executing an autonomous runway landing
majorAchievements: Accumulated over 3,774 total days in space across 7 secret long-duration missions
timeline: 2010-04-22: OTV-1 maiden launch on Atlas V
2022-11-12: OTV-6 landed after record-breaking 908-day flight
2023-12-28: OTV-7 launched on SpaceX Falcon Heavy into highly elliptical orbit

description: X-37B (OTV) is an uncrewed reusable spaceplane operated by the US Space Force. Built by Boeing, X-37B performs long-duration secret technology demonstration missions in orbit.
observationCapabilities: Autonomous Mach 25 Winged Re-entry & Runway Landing

name: LISA Pathfinder
instruments: LISA Technology Package (LTP - ESA Laser Interferometer)
ST7 Disturbance Reduction System (DRS - NASA Cold-Gas Micro-thrusters)
Two 4.6 cm Gold-Platinum Free-Falling Test Masses

Pave the way for the space-based gravitational wave observatory LISA
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated test mass free-fall acceleration noise 5 times lower than requirements, proving space-based gravitational wave detection is feasible
majorAchievements: Achieved quietest free-fall environment ever created by humanity
timeline: 2015-12-03: Launched on Vega from Kourou
2016-01-22: Arrived at Sun-Earth L1 orbit
2016-02-15: Test masses released into free fall
2017-06-30: Mission completed with outstanding success
interestingFacts: LISA Pathfinder measured the relative motion of two free-falling gold-platinum cubes to within sub-picometer precision (smaller than the diameter of an atom).
description: LISA Pathfinder was an ESA technology demonstrator that verified sub-picometer laser tracking of free-falling test masses in space, proving the concept for the upcoming LISA gravitational wave observatory.
primaryDiscoveries: Empirical Proof of Space Gravitational Wave Laser Detection

name: CAPSTONE (Cislunar Autonomous Positioning System Technology Operations and Navigation Experiment)
instruments: CAPS Autonomous Cross-link Radio Navigation Payload

Demonstrate autonomous spacecraft-to-spacecraft navigation (CAPS) without relying on Earth Deep Space Network

Successfully performed inter-satellite cross-link communication with NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)

timeline: 2022-06-28: Launched on Rocket Lab Electron from New Zealand
2022-11-13: Entered NRHO orbit around the Moon
2023-05-18: Completed primary 6-month NRHO navigation mission
interestingFacts: CAPSTONE is a microwave-oven-sized 12U CubeSat weighing only 25 kg that paved the path for NASA's billion-dollar Gateway station.
description: CAPSTONE is a 12U NASA CubeSat built by Terran Orbital and operated by Advanced Space. It became the first spacecraft to enter and validate the Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) for Gateway.

name: LightSail 2

Crowdfunded citizen-science technology demonstration by The Planetary Society

Winner of TIME Magazine Best Inventions of 2019
timeline: 2019-06-25: Launched on SpaceX Falcon Heavy STP-2
2019-07-23: Solar sail deployed successfully
2022-11-17: Burned up in Earth atmosphere after 3.5 years of solar sailing

description: LightSail 2 was a crowdfunded 3U CubeSat built by The Planetary Society. Deployed in 2019, it successfully demonstrated controlled solar sailing by using photon momentum to raise its orbit.
observationCapabilities: 32 m² Reflective Mylar Solar Sail Attitude Control
primaryDiscoveries: Pure Sunlight Orbital Apogee Raising (3.2 km gain)

2011-10-02: GLONASS-K next-generation satellite testing commenced

description: GLONASS is Russia's global navigation satellite system operated by Roscosmos and the Russian Aerospace Forces, providing global positioning and timing signals.

description: BeiDou (BDS-3) is China's global navigation satellite system operated by the CSNO. Featuring a hybrid constellation of MEO, GEO, and IGSO satellites, BDS-3 delivers sub-meter positioning and short-message messaging globally.

primaryDiscoveries: Hybrid Orbit Millimeter Positioning & Satellite SMS System
