2025-03-01: Mars gravity assist flyby
2026-12-01: Earth gravity assist flyby
2030-04-11: Target Jupiter orbit insertion and Europa flyby campaign start

description: Europa Clipper is NASA's flagship ocean world mission launched in October 2024 on Falcon Heavy. Europa Clipper will perform 49 close flybys of Europa down to 25 km altitude to investigate its subsurface ocean.
observationCapabilities: Dual-Frequency REASON Ice Sounding Radar & MASPEX Mass Spectrometry
primaryDiscoveries: Largest NASA Planetary Spacecraft Flawless Falcon Heavy Launch

4 Dual-Coaxial Rotor Arms (8 Rotors powered by MMRTG nuclear power)

Explore Shangri-La dune fields and Selk impact crater to sample organic prebiotic chemistry
Fly tens of kilometers between landing sites to investigate Titan's dense nitrogen/methane atmosphere and liquid hydrocarbon hydrologic cycle
majorDiscoveries: First mission to fly an octocopter rotorcraft across the surface of an outer Solar System moon
majorAchievements: NASA New Frontiers Program selection for Titan organic world exploration
timeline: 2028-07-01: Target launch window
2034-01-15: Target entry and landing on Saturn's moon Titan
interestingFacts: Titan has 4 times denser atmosphere than Earth and only 1/7th Earth's gravity, making human flight with artificial wings possible and allowing Dragonfly to fly easily using less power than on Earth.
description: Dragonfly is NASA's upcoming New Frontiers nuclear-powered rotorcraft lander. Flying across Saturn's moon Titan in 2034, Dragonfly will explore organic prebiotic chemistry across dune fields and impact craters.
observationCapabilities: Nuclear MMRTG Powered 8-Rotor Aerial Mobility & Laser Mass Spectrometry
primaryDiscoveries: First Nuclear Octocopter Outer Solar System Exploration Flight

name: Giotto
missionObjectives: Perform world's first close flyby of Comet Halley nucleus (within 600 km) during 1986 apparition
Capture first high-resolution optical photographs of a comet's icy nucleus
majorDiscoveries: Captured first close-up photographs of Comet Halley's dark peanut-shaped nucleus (15 x 8 km) spewing gas jets
Proved comet nucleus is 80% water ice covered in ultra-dark organic crust reflecting only 4% of light
majorAchievements: ESA's first deep-space mission; closest flyby of Comet Halley (596 km altitude on March 14, 1986)
First spacecraft to fly by two comets (Comet Halley in 1986 and Comet Grigg-Skjellerup in 1992)
timeline: 1985-07-02: Launched on Ariane 1 from Kourou
1986-03-14 00:03 UTC: Closest approach to Comet Halley (596 km), taking dust hit that disabled camera
1990-07-02: First Earth gravity assist by a deep-space probe
1992-07-10: Flew past Comet Grigg-Skjellerup at 200 km distance
interestingFacts: Giotto was named after 14th-century Florentine painter Giotto di Bondone, who depicted Comet Halley as the Star of Bethlehem in his 1301 fresco 'Adoration of the Magi'.
description: Giotto was ESA's historic first deep-space probe. On March 14, 1986, Giotto flew within 596 km of Comet Halley's nucleus, capturing the first close-up photographs of a comet core.
observationCapabilities: Halley Multicolour Camera 596km Nucleus Optical Imaging
primaryDiscoveries: First Close-up Photo of Comet Halley Nucleus & Dark Organic Shell

name: International Cometary Explorer (ICE / ISEE-3)
missionObjectives: Become world's first spacecraft stationed at Sun-Earth L1 halo orbit (as ISEE-3)
Execute orbital maneuvering past the Moon to fly through the tail of Comet Giacobini-Zinner as the world's first comet flyby mission
majorDiscoveries: Flew directly through the ion tail of Comet Giacobini-Zinner on Sept 11, 1985, confirming cometary magnetic field interaction
First spacecraft to use complex Earth-Moon gravity swingby trajectories to change orbits
majorAchievements: World's first spacecraft stationed at Sun-Earth L1 (1978)
World's first spacecraft to fly through a comet's tail (September 11, 1985)
timeline: 1978-08-12: Launched on Delta from Cape Canaveral into Sun-Earth L1 halo orbit
1982-06-10: Renamed ICE and maneuvers directed it toward lunar flybys
1985-09-11: Flew through tail of Comet Giacobini-Zinner at 7,800 km altitude
1986-03-28: Observed Comet Halley from 28 million km distance

description: ICE (originally ISEE-3) was a historic NASA/ESA space probe. Stationed at Sun-Earth L1 in 1978, it was later maneuvered past the Moon to perform the world's first comet tail flyby at Comet Giacobini-Zinner in 1985.
observationCapabilities: First L1 Halo Orbit Stationkeeping & Comet Ion Tail Plasma Flyby
primaryDiscoveries: World's First In-Situ Comet Tail Flyby (Sept 11, 1985)

name: NEAR Shoemaker (Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous)
missionObjectives: Perform world's first orbit and landing on a Near-Earth asteroid (433 Eros)
Determine asteroid mass, density, elemental composition, and surface regolith structure
majorDiscoveries: Returned 160,000 high-resolution images of 433 Eros, revealing a cratered 'peanut-shaped' S-type asteroid (34 x 11 km) covered in a deep layer of regolith dust
Determined Eros is an un-differentiated primitive chondritic asteroid with a bulk density of 2.67 g/cm³
majorAchievements: First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid (February 14, 2000)
First spacecraft to land on an asteroid (February 12, 2001)
timeline: 1996-02-17: Launched on Delta II from Cape Canaveral
1997-06-27: Flyby of main-belt asteroid 253 Mathilde
2000-02-14: Entered orbit around asteroid 433 Eros on Valentine's Day
2001-02-12: Historic soft landing on Eros surface at 1.9 m/s speed; transmitted signals for 16 days from surface

description: NEAR Shoemaker was a historic NASA Discovery mission built by JHU APL. It became the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid (433 Eros) in 2000 and the first to land on an asteroid on February 12, 2001.
observationCapabilities: 160,000 Multispectral Images & Unscheduled 1.9 m/s Asteroid Landing
primaryDiscoveries: First Asteroid Orbit & First Landing on an Asteroid (Feb 12, 2001)

name: Comet Interceptor
destination: Sun-Earth L2 / Dynamically New Comet or Interstellar Object
instruments: 3-Spacecraft Configuration (Main Spacecraft A, Probe B1 JAXA, Probe B2 ESA)
missionObjectives: Park at Sun-Earth L2 waiting for the discovery of a pristine 'dynamically new' comet originating directly from the Oort Cloud or an interstellar object (like 'Oumuamua)
Deploy 3 separate probe sub-spacecraft to fly by the target comet simultaneously from multiple angles
majorDiscoveries: First space mission designed to intercept a pristine Oort Cloud comet visiting the inner Solar System for the very first time in human history
majorAchievements: ESA Fast (F-class) mission selected in partnership with JAXA
timeline: 2029-01-01: Target launch window alongside ESA's ARIEL space telescope
2029-2032: Parked at Sun-Earth L2 awaiting astronomical comet discovery and dispatch
interestingFacts: Comet Interceptor will launch into space before its target comet is even discovered! It will wait at Sun-Earth L2 until astronomers spot a brand-new pristine comet heading toward the Sun.
description: Comet Interceptor is an innovative ESA/JAXA mission launching in 2029. Parked at Sun-Earth L2, it will wait for the discovery of a pristine Oort Cloud comet or interstellar visitor to execute a 3-probe flyby.
primaryDiscoveries: First Mission Designed to Intercept Un-Discovered Pristine Oort Comet

name: Pioneer Venus Orbiter (Pioneer 12)
missionObjectives: Perform first long-term global radar topographic mapping of Venus through its dense cloud cover
Monitor solar wind interaction with Venusian ionosphere over a complete 11-year solar cycle
majorDiscoveries: Mapped 93% of Venus's surface topography, discovering Ishtar Terra and Aphrodite Terra continent-like highlands
Discovered Venus's upper atmosphere lacks an intrinsic magnetic field and experiences extreme solar wind stripping
majorAchievements: Operated in Venus orbit for 14 years, completing 5,056 orbits
timeline: 1978-05-20: Launched on Atlas-Centaur from Cape Canaveral
1978-12-04: Entered orbit around Venus
1992-10-22: Burned up in Venus atmosphere upon propellant exhaustion
interestingFacts: Pioneer Venus Orbiter mapped Venus's topography through dense clouds for 14 years before finally burning up in Venus's atmosphere like a shooting star in 1992.
description: Pioneer Venus Orbiter was NASA's long-lived Venus mapping orbiter. Operational from 1978 to 1992, it produced the first global radar topographic map of Venus, discovering Ishtar Terra and Aphrodite Terra.
observationCapabilities: Orbital Radar Topographic Mapping & UV Spectrometry
primaryDiscoveries: First Global Radar Map of Venus (Ishtar & Aphrodite Terra)

name: Pioneer Venus Multiprobe (Pioneer 13)
instruments: Large Probe (Sounder Probe with Neutral Mass Spectrometer)
Three Small Probes (North, Day, Night Probes with Nephelometers)
missionObjectives: Deploy 4 independent probe capsules into Venus's atmosphere simultaneously at different locations
Measure atmospheric composition, cloud layer density, and thermal structure down to the surface
majorDiscoveries: Discovered high concentration of primordial argon-36 and neon in Venus atmosphere, indicating different planetary accretion history than Earth
Day probe survived impact on surface and transmitted data for 67 minutes from Venusian soil
majorAchievements: World's first four-probe simultaneous atmospheric entry mission
timeline: 1978-08-08: Launched on Atlas-Centaur from Cape Canaveral
1978-12-09: Released Large Probe and 3 Small Probes into Venus atmosphere
1978-12-09: Day Probe survived surface impact, transmitting data for 67 minutes
interestingFacts: One of the unarmored 'Small Probes' survived impacting Venus at 35 km/h, continuing to radio temperature and pressure data back to Earth from the scorching 460°C surface for 67 minutes.
description: Pioneer Venus Multiprobe was NASA's multi-capsule atmospheric mission. On December 9, 1978, it released 4 probes into Venus's atmosphere, measuring cloud layers and primordial atmospheric gases.

name: Venera 14
instruments: Soil Drill & Hermetic X-ray Fluorescence Chamber
missionObjectives: Perform sister soft landing to Venera 13 at Phoebe Regio plain
Capture 360-degree color panoramas and drill ocean-floor-like oceanic tholeiite basalt rocks
majorDiscoveries: Returned vibrant 360° color surface photos showing yellow-orange skies and flat sheet-like volcanic basalt rocks
Drilled and analyzed rock sample, confirming composition resembles Earth's oceanic crustal tholeiites
majorAchievements: Operated for 57 minutes on Venus surface in 465°C heat and 94 atmospheres pressure
timeline: 1981-11-04: Launched on Proton-K from Baikonur
1982-03-05 03:25 UTC: Soft landed at Phoebe Regio (950 km from Venera 13); operated for 57 minutes
interestingFacts: Venera 14 landed on flat volcanic basalt sheets that looked like flagstone paving stones laid out by ancient stonemasons.
description: Venera 14 was a historic Soviet Venus lander mission. Landing at Phoebe Regio on March 5, 1982, Venera 14 captured high-resolution color surface panoramas and analyzed oceanic-type volcanic basalts.
observationCapabilities: 360° Color Panoramic Facsimile & Tholeiite Basalt Soil Spectroscopy
primaryDiscoveries: Oceanic Tholeiite Basalt Surface Composition Confirmation

name: Vega 1 (Venus-Halley Mission 1)

instruments: 3.5m Helium Aerostat Balloon & Transmitter Payload (French CNES)
TVS (Television System Camera for Comet Halley)

Use Venus gravity assist to redirect main spacecraft to fly by Comet Halley
majorDiscoveries: Vega 1 balloon floated 54 km above Venus for 46 hours across 11,600 km, measuring violent 240 km/h winds and down-drafts
Flew past Comet Halley on March 6, 1986 at 8,890 km, capturing 500 photos of the comet nucleus
majorAchievements: World's first robotic balloon exploration of another planet's atmosphere (June 11, 1985)
timeline: 1984-12-15: Launched on Proton-K from Baikonur
1985-06-11: Deployed lander and balloon into Venus atmosphere
1986-03-06: Historic flyby of Comet Halley nucleus at 8,890 km distance
interestingFacts: Vega 1 deployed a 3.5-meter helium balloon into Venus's clouds that drifted across the night side of Venus for 2 days, tracked by 20 radio telescopes across Earth.
description: Vega 1 was an ambitious Soviet space mission. In June 1985, it deployed a lander and the world's first atmospheric balloon into Venus's clouds, then flew past Comet Halley in March 1986.
observationCapabilities: 3.5m Helium Aerostat Cloud Drift & Comet Nucleus Optical TV System
primaryDiscoveries: World's First Planetary Atmospheric Balloon Deployment (46 Hours)

Detected ~155 kg of water vapor and ice ejected into the sunlight during impact plume
majorAchievements: Definitive proof of pure water ice inside permanently shadowed craters at the Moon's South Pole
timeline: 2009-06-18: Launched alongside LRO on Atlas V
2009-10-09 11:31 UTC: Centaur upper stage struck Cabeus crater at 2.5 km/s
2009-10-09 11:35 UTC: Shepherd spacecraft flew through plume, transmitting real-time infrared spectra before impacting 4 minutes later
interestingFacts: LCROSS used its own spent Centaur rocket stage as a 2.3-ton kinetic bullet to blast open the frozen floor of Cabeus crater.
description: LCROSS was a NASA mission launched with LRO. On October 9, 2009, LCROSS slammed its spent Centaur rocket stage into Cabeus crater, proving pure water ice exists at the Moon's South Pole.
observationCapabilities: In-Plume Multi-Band Infrared/UV Spectroscopy of 10km Ejecta Plume
primaryDiscoveries: Definitive Confirmation of Pure Polar Lunar Water Ice (5.6% by Mass)

name: Beresheet
instruments: Lunar Arch Disc (30-million page digital time capsule)
missionObjectives: Perform world's first privately funded commercial lander mission to soft land on the Moon
Measure local magnetic field at Mare Serenitatis
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated low-cost commercial lunar transit and lunar orbit insertion on a $100M budget
majorAchievements: First private commercial entity to enter orbit around the Moon (April 4, 2019)
timeline: 2019-02-22: Launched on Falcon 9 as secondary payload
2019-04-04: Successfully entered lunar orbit
2019-04-11 19:23 UTC: Main engine failure at 150m altitude resulted in hard crash landing at Mare Serenitatis
interestingFacts: Beresheet carried a digital time capsule containing the entire English Wikipedia, the Hebrew Bible, and thousands of dehydrated tardigrades (water bears).
description: Beresheet was a pioneering Israeli commercial lunar lander built by SpaceIL and IAI. In April 2019, it became the first privately funded spacecraft to orbit the Moon.
observationCapabilities: Low-Cost Commercial Trajectory & NASA Laser Retroreflector
primaryDiscoveries: First Privately Funded Spacecraft to Orbit the Moon

name: Hakuto-R Mission 1 (ispace M1)
instruments: Rashid Rover (10 kg UAE Lunar Rover)
missionObjectives: Perform Japan's first commercial lunar lander mission to Atlas Crater
Deploy UAE's Rashid rover and JAXA Sora-Q transformable ball robot
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated 4-month low-energy transfer orbit from Earth to lunar orbit for commercial payloads
majorAchievements: First commercial lunar lander developed by a Japanese company
timeline: 2022-12-11: Launched on Falcon 9 alongside NASA Lunar Flashlight
2023-03-21: Successfully entered lunar orbit
2023-04-25 16:40 UTC: Altitude sensor miscalculation over crater rim caused lander to run out of fuel 5 km up and hard land in Atlas Crater
interestingFacts: Hakuto-R carried the UAE's 10 kg Rashid rover, which was designed to take the highest resolution photos ever taken of lunar dust.
description: Hakuto-R Mission 1 was a commercial lunar lander built by Japanese company ispace. Launched on Falcon 9 in 2022, it successfully entered lunar orbit before a descent sensor error caused a hard landing in Atlas crater.
observationCapabilities: Low-Energy Transfer Flight & Multimodal Payload Delivery
primaryDiscoveries: First Japanese Commercial Lunar Lander Orbital Entry

name: GOES-16 (GOES-R / Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite)
instruments: EXIS (Extreme Ultraviolet and X-ray Irradiance Sensors)
missionObjectives: Provide continuous 30-second high-resolution weather, hurricane, and wildfire imaging over the Americas
Map total lightning flash activity and monitor solar flares / space weather hazards from GEO
majorDiscoveries: First operational geostationary satellite to continuously map total in-cloud and cloud-to-ground lightning flashes
Pioneered 30-second rapid scan imagery for severe thunderstorm and tornado forecasting
majorAchievements: Flagship satellite of NOAA's next-generation GOES-R weather constellation (GOES-East)
timeline: 2016-11-19: Launched on Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
2017-12-18: Declared fully operational as GOES-East
interestingFacts: GOES-16's Lightning Mapper captures 500 images per second, tracking lightning bolts across the entire Western Hemisphere day and night.
description: GOES-16 is NOAA's flagship geostationary environmental satellite operating as GOES-East at 75.2°W. Equipped with the ABI imager and GLM lightning mapper, it provides real-time 30-second severe weather and hurricane tracking.
observationCapabilities: 30-Second 16-Channel Advanced Baseline Imager & Continuous Lightning Mapping
primaryDiscoveries: Continuous Geostationary Lightning & 30-Second Tornado Rapid Scanning

name: Suomi NPP (National Polar-orbiting Partnership)
instruments: VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite - Day/Night Band)
CERES (Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System)
missionObjectives: Provide essential global daily atmospheric temperature/moisture soundings for 3- to 7-day numerical weather prediction models
Capture ultra-sensitive night-time low-light imagery of Earth's city lights, auroras, and moonlit clouds via VIIRS Day/Night Band
majorDiscoveries: VIIRS Day/Night Band captured famous 'Black Marble' composite images showing human artificial lights across all continents
Monitored global wildfire emissions and sea surface temperature anomalies continuously for 14+ years
majorAchievements: Bridge satellite mission connecting NASA's EOS fleet (Terra/Aqua) to NOAA's JPSS series
timeline: 2011-10-28: Launched on Delta II from Vandenberg
2012-01-25: Famous 'Blue Marble 2012' composite image released worldwide
interestingFacts: Suomi NPP's VIIRS camera is so sensitive at night that it can photograph a single city streetlight or fishing boat light from 824 km up in space.
description: Suomi NPP is a joint NOAA/NASA polar-orbiting environmental satellite. Operational since 2011, its VIIRS imager captures high-precision daily atmospheric profiles and iconic night-time 'Black Marble' low-light imagery.
observationCapabilities: VIIRS Ultra-Sensitive Nighttime Day/Night Band & Microwave Sounding
primaryDiscoveries: Iconic 'Black Marble' Earth Night Lights Map & Global Wildfire Tracking

name: Mars 3 Lander & Orbiter
instruments: PrOP-M Micro-Rover (4.5 kg tethered walking ski-rover)
missionObjectives: Perform world's first soft landing on Mars surface and deploy PrOP-M tethered micro-rover
Map Mars surface and atmosphere from 12-day elliptical orbit
majorDiscoveries: Soft landed on Mars during fierce global dust storm, transmitting partial facsimile frame before signal cut off after 14.5 seconds
majorAchievements: World's first spacecraft to achieve a survivable soft landing on Mars (December 2, 1971)
timeline: 1971-05-28: Launched on Proton-K from Baikonur
1971-12-02 13:52 UTC: Soft landed at Terra Sirenum (45°S, 158°W); transmitted 14.5 seconds of data before signal lost
interestingFacts: Mars 3 carried PrOP-M, a 4.5 kg micro-rover that moved using two flat skis on tethered cables—making it the world's first rover designed for another planet.
description: Mars 3 was a historic Soviet space probe that accomplished the world's first soft landing on Mars on December 2, 1971, touching down at Terra Sirenum during a global dust storm.
observationCapabilities: Tethered Ski Micro-Rover & Soft Aeroshell Heatshield Landing
primaryDiscoveries: World's First Soft Landing on Mars (Dec 2, 1971)

name: Freedom 7 (Mercury-Redstone 3)
missionObjectives: Perform America's first human spaceflight, placing astronaut Alan Shepard into space
Demonstrate manual pilot control of spacecraft attitude in zero gravity
majorDiscoveries: Proved human astronauts can manually control spacecraft attitude in space weightlessness without physical impairment
majorAchievements: First American in space (Alan Shepard, May 5, 1961)
timeline: 1961-05-05 14:34 UTC: Launched on Redstone rocket from LC-5
1961-05-05 14:39 UTC: Reached apogee of 187.5 km (116.5 miles), entering space
1961-05-05 14:49 UTC: Splashdown in Atlantic Ocean after 15-minute 22-second flight
interestingFacts: Sitting on top of the rocket during hours of delays, Alan Shepard famously radioed launch control: 'Please dear God, don't let me screw up!'
description: Freedom 7 was America's historic first crewed spaceflight capsule. Piloted by astronaut Alan Shepard on May 5, 1961, Freedom 7 reached an altitude of 187.5 km in a 15-minute suborbital flight.
observationCapabilities: 70mm Optical Periscope & Manual Thruster Pitch/Yaw Steering
primaryDiscoveries: First American Human Spaceflight (Alan Shepard, May 5, 1961)

name: Gemini 8 (Gemini VIII)
missionObjectives: Perform world's first physical space docking between two orbiting spacecraft (Gemini 8 and Agena Target Vehicle)
Execute extravehicular activity (EVA) spacewalk
majorDiscoveries: Demonstrated orbital rendezvous and physical docking in space
Command pilot Neil Armstrong demonstrated legendary composure during emergency stuck-thruster spin, regaining control using re-entry thrusters
majorAchievements: World's first docking of two spacecraft in space (March 16, 1966)
timeline: 1966-03-16 16:41 UTC: Launched with Neil Armstrong and David Scott aboard
1966-03-16 22:14 UTC: Docked successfully with Agena Target Vehicle
1966-03-16 22:45 UTC: Stuck OAMS thruster caused violent 1-revolution-per-second spin; Armstrong undocked and stabilized vehicle
1966-03-17 03:22 UTC: Emergency splashdown in Pacific Ocean
interestingFacts: Neil Armstrong's rapid reflexes saved Gemini 8 from spinning out of control at nearly 60 RPM in total darkness over the Pacific, proving his cool head for Apollo 11.
description: Gemini 8 was NASA's historic crewed spaceflight commanded by Neil Armstrong with pilot David Scott. On March 16, 1966, Gemini 8 performed the world's first space docking with an Agena Target Vehicle.
observationCapabilities: Radar Target Docking Adapter & Manual OAMS Thruster Docking

name: Salyut 1 (DOS-1)
missionObjectives: Construct and operate the world's first inhabited orbital space station
Test long-duration human space habitation, solar UV astronomy, and agricultural plant growth in zero-G
majorDiscoveries: Proved humans can inhabit, work, and perform complex scientific research inside an orbital space station for 23 consecutive days (Soyuz 11 crew)
majorAchievements: World's first space station in human history (Launched April 19, 1971)
timeline: 1971-04-19: Launched on Proton-K from Baikonur
1971-06-07: Soyuz 11 crew docked successfully, inhabiting station for 23 days
1971-10-11: Controlled re-entry into Pacific Ocean after 175 days in orbit
interestingFacts: Salyut 1 was the spark for all future space stations—including Skylab, Mir, Tiangong, and the International Space Station.
description: Salyut 1 was the world's first space station. Launched by the Soviet Union on April 19, 1971, Salyut 1 hosted the Soyuz 11 crew for 23 days, pioneering long-duration orbital laboratory research.
observationCapabilities: Orion-1 400mm UV Space Telescope & 23-Day Crew Habitation Module
primaryDiscoveries: World's First Inhabited Orbital Space Station

name: Shenzhou 5
instruments: Orbital Module Earth Reconnaissance Camera Payload
Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS)
missionObjectives: Perform China's historic first crewed spaceflight, carrying taikonaut Yang Liwei into Earth orbit
Demonstrate indigenous human spaceflight launch, orbital maneuvering, and safe re-entry recovery
majorDiscoveries: Proved China's independent capability to launch, maintain, and safely return human astronauts from Earth orbit
majorAchievements: China became 3rd nation in human history to independently launch a human into space (October 15, 2003)
timeline: 2003-10-15 01:00 UTC: Launched on Long March 2F from Jiuquan carrying Yang Liwei
2003-10-16 06:23 UTC: Landed safely in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia after 14 orbits (21 hours 22 minutes)
interestingFacts: Yang Liwei displayed the flags of both the People's Republic of China and the United Nations while in orbit aboard Shenzhou 5.
description: Shenzhou 5 was China's historic maiden crewed spaceflight mission. Launched on October 15, 2003, carrying taikonaut Yang Liwei, China became the third nation to independently send a human into space.
observationCapabilities: Crewed ECLSS Life Support & Orbital Module Earth Reconnaissance
primaryDiscoveries: First Chinese Human Spaceflight (Yang Liwei, Oct 15, 2003)

name: VERITAS (Venus Emissivity, Radio Science, InSAR, Topography, and Spectroscopy)
instruments: VISAR (Venus Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar - 30m resolution 3D topography)
VEM (Venus Emissivity Mapper - DLR surface rock composition mapper)
Gravity Science Experiment (Ka-band internal structure probe)
missionObjectives: Create first 3D global topographic map of Venus at 30m spatial resolution (100 times higher resolution than Magellan)
Search for active volcanic eruptions, lava flows, and plate-tectonic-like continent rift deformation
majorDiscoveries: Designed to answer why Venus (Earth's twin planet) evolved into a scorching uninhabitable greenhouse world while Earth became lush and temperate
majorAchievements: NASA Discovery Program selection for high-resolution Venus radar exploration
timeline: 2031-01-01: Target launch window
2031-08-15: Target Venus orbit entry and aerobraking phase
interestingFacts: VERITAS will map Venus with synthetic aperture radar so sharp it can detect active volcanic eruptions occurring live on Venus's surface.
description: VERITAS is NASA JPL's upcoming Discovery orbiter mission to Venus. Utilizing synthetic aperture radar (VISAR) and infrared mapping (VEM), VERITAS will create 3D 30-meter topographic maps of Venus.
observationCapabilities: VISAR 30m 3D Synthetic Aperture Radar & VEM Emissivity Spectroscopy
primaryDiscoveries: 100x Resolution 3D Topographic & Active Volcano Mapping Capability
